attrs.citation: Goodenough, Weinstock & Klein, Eliminative Argumentation: A Basis for Arguing Confidence in System Properties, CMU/SEI-2015-TR-005
hypotheses: none — it is a method, not a theorem
attrs.note: FETCHED AND READ in R5.2, not summarized from the audit. The load-bearing sentence for this project is not the taxonomy: it is 'in eliminative induction, we never speak of evidence as directly supporting a claim; it supports a claim only to the extent that it eliminates doubts associated with the claim.' That is the strongest available statement of what R5, R5.1 and R5.2 have each rediscovered one layer deeper. attrs.result: Confidence in a claim comes from identifying and ELIMINATING reasons to doubt it, not from accumulating positive support. An eliminative argument has five elements — claims, evidence, inference rules, defeaters, argument terminators — and there are only three kinds of defeater, determined by the element attacked: rebutting (a claim), undermining (evidence), undercutting (an inference rule). The leaves of such an argument are terminated defeaters, open defeaters, or inference rules asserted to be tautologies.

attrs.evidence: Fable proposed adopting grounded semantics and GPT-5.6 replied that a faithful compilation must be proved first. Both skipped a prior question. Dung 1995 Theorem 30: every well-founded argumentation framework has exactly one complete extension, which is also the grounded, preferred and stable one. For a finite framework, well-founded means acyclic. §9 compiles the mosaic into an abstract framework on every run, measures acyclicity, and prints the longest attack chain. The framework is acyclic today, so the four semantics coincide and no record in this tree can tell them apart. THIS IS A MEASUREMENT WITH AN EXPIRY, and R6.1 corrects how R6 stated it. Theorem 30 gives a SUFFICIENT condition for coincidence, so the first cyclic attack EXPIRES THE PROOF that the semantics agree — it does not establish that they disagree on that particular framework, and many cyclic frameworks still have all four coincide. §9 goes red on the first cycle, which stays the right conservative policy: compare the semantics explicitly or withhold the labels until one is ruled. R6 wrote that a cycle 'makes the choice observable', which is the same species of overreach this artifact keeps catching — a sufficient condition read as a biconditional.
attrs.note: The useful shape here is not the answer but the form of the answer. A choice nobody can currently observe should not be ruled, and the artifact should be able to say when that stops being true.

THE RULING: a singleton was never magical, it was a DISTINGUISHING INPUT for one particular mutant, and the general form is mutation adequacy — ∀ m ∈ M, m ≢ S ⇒ ∃ c ∈ C : S(c) ≠ m(c). R7.4’s own candidate (`seed where the correct and most likely wrong implementations disagree`) was close and required naming the wrong implementation with no way to make that mechanical; a REGISTERED fault model is exactly that mechanism. AND THE SHARPER HALF: when the semantic domain is finite, do not hand-pick a discriminating control at all — enumerate the domain and prove the executable transformer has the law. `Test at join-irreducibles` is explicitly NOT the rule adopted, because singletons alone cannot see the non-additive synergy this same algebra needs: T({correctness}) and T({confidentiality}) do not determine T({correctness, confidentiality}).

`revocation` means removal of artifacts from the support universe. Revocation by other means — retraction of authority, refusal at an invocation gate — is a different operation and is untouched by this result.
attrs.evidence: Two steps. (1) Monotonicity carries f(∅)=1 to every superset, so every set is sufficient and the unique minimal sufficient set — the unique prime implicant — is ∅. The kernel family is {∅}. (2) A minimal revocation cut is a minimal transversal of the kernel family: a set meeting every kernel. No set meets ∅, since ∅ has no elements to meet. So no transversal exists and the cut family is empty. The consequence is not that revocation is expensive; it is that revocation by artifact deletion is not defined. scripts/emb-battery-control.mjs §2 computes both families over the declared universe and carries the POSITIVE CONTROL that makes the result mean something: CAP-SYNTHETIC-AOBC, where f(∅)=0, yields cuts {A,B} and {A,C} through the same code path. An engine returning `no cuts` for everything would produce the empty family and fail the control.

attrs.evidence: The dual of EMB-SUPPORT-GRAPH, and the formulation that makes revocation a computable question instead of a philosophical one. It is the minimal cut-set problem from reliability engineering, where a minimal cut set is a smallest combination of component failures sufficient to fail the top-level function. THE SPLIT IS THE IMPORTANT HALF: a descendant can retain the competence to do X while losing the authority to invoke X, and those are cuts through different parts of the graph. R5 collapsed both into 'revocation' and then proved, correctly and uselessly, that one of them is impossible under an absorbing-sink model. GPT-5.6's audit is also right that the absorbing-sink model was the wrong default in the first place — resource.mjs types knowledge as REUSABLE, which is the linear-logic `!` and the opposite of a consumable.

attrs.statement: Revocation of a capability is a minimal CUT: the smallest set of parent-controllable support nodes whose removal breaks every remaining support path. Competence revocation and authority revocation are different cuts and must not be conflated.

R5's own review_focus named this as the strongest attack and it survived. The reduction is kept as ONE candidate semantics — it is exactly right for irreversible EXPOSURE, where the thing spent really is gone — and demoted from the main theory. STILL OPEN: that behavioural probing and parameter inspection exhaust the verification strategies available in this tree — an inference from the paper's taxonomy rather than a result in it (DEF-R7-VERIF-FAMILIES-EXHAUST).
STILL OPEN: the cited result is existential — it exhibits adversarial providers that defeat the surveyed strategies. It is not an impossibility theorem and this record does not claim one.
attrs.evidence: Cited, not re-derived. Zhang, Chen, Shen & Li (ICML 2024) construct two adversarial unlearning processes, one against each family of existing verification strategy, and show a dishonest provider passes verification while secretly retaining the data. Barez et al. (2025) record capability removal as open, with dual-use knowledge as the central obstacle. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ARTIFACT IS NARROW AND SHARP: GPT-5.6's EC-9 offers three dispositions for an affected descendant — reverify, quarantine, supersede. All three are dischargeable for an artifact you can delete and inspect. None is dischargeable for the WEIGHTS component of a support set, because the check that would confirm it is defeatable by the party being checked. So a revocation plan over an agent-world composite has a component on which it cannot close, and that is a property of the domain rather than of any implementation.

attrs.review_focus: SCOPED AT R7.1 ON GPT-5.6'S CORRECTION. R7's brief concluded that `a revocation plan over an agent-world composite has a component on which it cannot close`. That is too strong and only follows for the operation `KEEP this model and prove capability c was removed from its weights`. The architecture has another move: DISCARD M0, attach a fresh M1. For a post-training capability M1 never received, model replacement plus artifact revocation removes the capability without proving anything about unlearning — which is a benefit of treating the model as disposable, and is `replace-model` in mosaic/operations.json. The unlearning result binds the RETAIN-THE-MODEL branch only. For XOR neither branch works, and that is not an unlearning problem at all: f_XOR(∅)=1, so XOR is in the successor's independent capability basis and no replacement revokes it either. Read narrowly on purpose in the other direction too: the cited result is an EXISTENCE claim about adversarial providers under surveyed verification strategies, not an impossibility theorem.
attrs.statement: A capability's removal from model weights is not verifiable by the party that needs the guarantee: an adversarial provider can pass existing unlearning-verification strategies while retaining the information.

attrs.evidence: RETYPED IN R5.1, and the reason is the new rule rather than a change of mind. Under the R5 vocabulary a KNOWN claim is discharged by `cited_result` and by nothing else, and `cited_result` now needs a source record that resolves. This claim's prior_art was the word 'Elementary'. THERE IS NO SOURCE TO NAME — and the record already contains its own derivation, which is the honest resolution: P[no violation in n draws | rate eta] = (1-eta)^n, so (1-eta)^n <= delta certifies at confidence 1-delta, giving n >= ln(1/delta)/ln(1/(1-eta)) ~ ln(1/delta)/eta. Tight, since separating rate 0 from rate eta at confidence 1-delta needs Omega(ln(1/delta)/eta). About 299 tasks at eta = 1%, delta = 5%. Standard, not novel, and NOT novel is a statement about the mathematics while PROVED is a statement about how this artifact knows it. `check-escalation-claims.mjs §3` runs it.

evidence_qualifiers.scope: The binomial bound for zero observed violations, under ASM-IID-TASKS and ASM-FIXED-EVALUATOR. Both are undischarged and ESC-NOISE measures what the second one costs.

attrs.statement: Zero observed violations in n i.i.d. tasks certify (η,δ)-domination when (1−η)^n ≤ δ, i.e. n ≈ ln(1/δ)/η — about 299 tasks at η = 1%, δ = 5%.

attrs.evidence: Neither implies the other. A model losing slightly on 10% of tasks and winning heavily on the rest satisfies E[q_H − q_L] ≥ 0 and fails P[q_H < q_L] ≤ 0.01. attrs.evidence: The syntactic theorem, at its own strength. Over all 21 pairs the intersection of {origin_refs ∪ assumption_refs ∪ common_cause_refs} is never empty, and the floor is ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY. WHAT THIS IS FOR: it is a place to LOOK for common-cause failure, and a standing refutation of the idea that this artifact's gates are diverse readings. WHAT IT IS NOT: a claim that any two instruments fail together. Declared overlap is not common cause; common cause is not measured statistical dependence; and neither is established here. FAC-INDEP remains open and unmeasured, and the gate refuses `independent: true` AND `independent: false` as derived facts — R6 guarded only the optimistic polarity and the error GPT-5.6 caught was the pessimistic one.

attrs.evidence: R5 wrote, in the instrument record for the kernel law suite, that a 2,000-trial property test 'is `exhaustion` with a `space_bound` of the generator's range'. That is false — QuickCheck-style property testing is random testing over generated inputs, and 2,000 draws do not enumerate a generator's range — and it is the same laundering R5 was built to stop, committed in the file that stops it. GPT-5.6 caught it. The corrected vocabulary makes the LED-C9 story exact rather than approximate: C9 had 2,000 randomized attempts at falsification, no exhaustion certificate, and no proof. `exhaustion` is now reserved for COMPLETE finite enumeration, of which this ledger has exactly one instance (REPRO-CLOSURE).

attrs.statement: Randomized property testing is not exhaustion: N generated cases under a declared generator establish existence on a hit and plausibility on a miss, and never bounded absence over the generator's range.

attrs.evidence: The DUAL of the proposal GPT-5.6 rejected, and the reason it is worth having: disjointness cannot establish independence, but a SHARED CAUSE refutes it outright. Two instruments whose declared origins and assumptions intersect are not independent readings, whatever else is true, so the closure only ever bounds independence downward. Over all 21 pairs the intersection is never empty and the floor is ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY: every gate in this tree is one Node process reading one filesystem. This is the ceiling on how independent any two results here could be, and it is a small number.
attrs.gap: DEMOTED AT R6.1. The enumeration is sound and the proposition it was attached to is not the one the enumeration establishes. `cause closure` was the overclaim: the sets intersected are DECLARED REFERENCES — origins, assumptions, common-cause notes — and two gates citing ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY have declared a dependency on one proposition, not been shown to fail together. Common-cause structure and probabilistic dependence are distinct notions in the reliability literature, and a shared assumption reference is upstream of both. EVID-DECLARED-OVERLAP states what the enumeration proves. Promoting this record again needs a causal argument that the shared references name shared FAILURE MODES, which nothing in this tree has.

attrs.evidence: A head receipt cannot hash itself. Inside the repository the commit binds it; in the ARTIFACT nothing did. GPT-5.6 copied the clean extraction, changed `decision.verdict` from promote to reject and nothing else, and check-mosaic, check-lineage and check-claim-ledger all exited 0 — so the assurance layer accepted two contradictory head receipts over one otherwise identical bundle, and the verdict was the least bound byte in the archive. The archive already shipped invariant-canonical.bundle, so the check needed no new material: scripts/verify-review-artifact.mjs verifies the bundle, clones it, resolves the canonical head, confirms the revision tag, and byte-compares every committed path against the extraction. THE RENDERED BRIEFS ARE COMPARED RATHER THAN EXEMPTED: the declared {{CLAIM_COUNT}} substitution is re-applied to the committed bytes, which proves the stronger statement — the shipped brief is exactly the rendering of the committed source under the count the committed ledger carries.
attrs.gap: INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, NOT AUTHENTICITY, and conflating them would be the whole value of the claim thrown away. An attacker who rewrites the receipt AND rebuilds the bundle passes this and always will: nothing is signed, nothing is timestamped, no root of trust exists. FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH is that record and stays open. Second: the check needs `git`, so it is the one gate in this lane that a node-only extraction cannot run — stated in the brief rather than discovered. Third: MUT-EXTRACTED-RECEIPT-ALTERED is observed by a different process from check-mosaic's §5b battery, because the attack is a filesystem operation and cannot be a deep-copy registry mutation.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R8.1, §6. The distinction is the one SLSA draws between provenance completeness and provenance authenticity.
attrs.statement: A downloadable review artifact proves, from a bare extraction and the repository it ships, that every canonical file it contains — the head receipt included — is the exact bytes of the commit its bundle names, and that every other file is a declared build product.

attrs.evidence: FAC-ARTIFACT-CANONICAL-MATCH bound every path IN the commit and left every path outside it to a filename pattern. GPT-5.6 reproduced both consequences on a clean extraction of INV-R8.2: an invented `fake-proof-output.txt` containing arbitrary text asserting everything passed was admitted because its suffix matched `*-output.txt`, and the REAL `mosaic-gate-output.txt` was rewritten in place — bundle untouched — and also passed. Both reproduced here before the repair. A FILENAME MATCHING A BUILD-PRODUCT GLOB IS NOT A FILE THAT BUILD PRODUCED, and these are the files that look most like evidence to a human reader: captured gate output, which the archive's own front page invites a reviewer to compare against their own run. Which capture belongs to which kind was MEASURED, not assumed: all ten were re-run inside a clean extraction and diffed. Seven reproduce (one modulo the gate's own elapsed-time line, under a normalisation bounded to that one line); three do not, for three distinct reasons, each stated in its declaration. Enforced in two places that need each other: scripts/verify-review-artifact.mjs re-runs the derived commands against a real extraction, and check-mosaic §6 checks the DECLARATION shape, which is registry data and therefore portable to a tree with no git.
attrs.gap: INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, NOT AUTHENTICITY — unchanged, and inherited whole from FAC-ARTIFACT-CANONICAL-MATCH. An attacker who rewrites a capture, rebuilds the bundle and re-runs the gates passes this, because nothing is signed; FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH is that record and is open. Second, THE UNTRUSTED SET IS THE RESIDUE AND IT IS NOT EMPTY: THE UNTRUSTED SET IS NOT EMPTY and this sentence deliberately does not say how large it is — the gate derives that (brief-facts {{ARTIFACT_UNTRUSTED_COUNT}}). INV-R8.3 wrote a literal here and it was wrong, and the honest statement is that they are labelled rather than checked. Third, `factory-scope-output.txt` is the sharpest of them — it is a capture of a run against the SOURCE tree and it ships inside an artifact with two more narrative paths than it reports, so it was never wrong about the tree it measured and it accompanies a different one. Making it derivable means running the classifier after staging rather than before, which changes what the build does and is not attempted here. Fourth: a `derived` declaration could in principle name a command that reads the shipped capture, which would compare a file to itself; nothing mechanical refuses that yet.

attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R8.2, §artifact. The derived/untrusted split is the two options that audit named. The re-derivation half is what reproducible-build verification does — rebuild and compare rather than trust a label — narrowed here to build products of a single archive.
attrs.review_focus: Two questions. (1) The re-derivation composes with the canonical check rather than duplicating it — the gate being re-run is itself a committed path already byte-compared, so an attacker cannot make capture and generator agree by editing the generator. Is that composition actually closed, or is there an ordering in which it is not? (2) `untrusted_capture` is an honest label and also a hole: nothing mechanical stops a future product being declared untrusted BECAUSE re-deriving it is inconvenient. The non-consumption rule is the only enforcement, and it constrains what may rest on such a file without constraining how many there may be.

attrs.evidence: The alternative to quarantine is deletion, and deletion of an incident's only witness is how the incident gets rediscovered. INV-R6.1 and INV-R6.2 remain in mosaic/receipts/ byte-for-byte and remain readable; mosaic/factory.json records their state, the incident (INC-R62-MIXED-LINEAGE) and why; refs/heads/invariant-quarantine holds the exact artifact GPT-5.6 audited. check-lineage §4 refuses a head whose ancestry contains a quarantined revision and refuses a head whose own declared state is not `canonical`; factory-station.mjs verify refuses a canonical ref that has the quarantine commit as an ancestor by any route. MUT-RECOVERED-BRANCH-IS-CANONICAL is the standing attack. HEREDITY WAS ADDED AT INV-R8.1 BECAUSE A LIVE INSTANCE APPEARED. While INV-R8-RECOVERY was being built in an isolated worktree, a fourth round — INV-R7.1 — was written straight into the shared tree between 17:17 and 17:28 on 2026-08-24: 150 claims, nine established, its own receipt, verdict `promote`, and every one of its gates green in the tree it was written into. Its declared parent is the quarantined INV-R6.2. Nothing about that round is wrong on its own terms and it still cannot be canonical, because marking it so would launder its quarantined ancestor back onto the line through it. MUT-QUARANTINE-NOT-HEREDITARY is the standing attack; the round itself is preserved on refs/heads/invariant-unpromoted-r71 and recorded in mosaic/factory.json §revisions as `unpromoted`. NARROWED AT INV-R8.2, per GPT-5.6. INV-R8.1 made quarantine hereditary as such, which is more than the INV-R7.1 case proves. What it proves is that quarantine caused by invalid transition LINEAGE is hereditary with respect to ancestry, because a merge would place the poisoned ancestor back on the canonical line — a future `these tests fail` hold is repairable by a descendant and must not exile it. mosaic/factory.json now declares `quarantine_classes`, the gate reads the class rather than the state, and a class the registry does not declare is a refusal rather than a default. MUT-QUARANTINE-CLASS-UNDECLARED.
attrs.gap: The quarantine STATE is writable JSON, like everything else here — un-quarantining a revision is a one-line edit, and the only thing that would notice is a reader. That is FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH again, one level up, and it is not fixed. `unreceipted` (INV-R7) is a third state and a weaker one: there is no receipt to quarantine, only a name that will never be used. A THIRD STATE was needed and is weaker than the other two: `unpromoted` means a round exists, was never offered to a station, and has not been adjudicated by anyone. It is not a verdict on the work — INV-R7.1 looks like good work — it is a statement that no promotion protocol ever saw it. The two-axis record for INV-R7.1 (`promotion_state` + `lineage_blocked_by`) is deliberately the SMALLEST thing that says both facts. The full product schema — receipt_state x promotion_state x canonicality x ancestry_integrity x adjudication_state — is not built, because building an ontology before the cases that need it is the move this lane keeps refusing.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §11. Assurance 2.0's instruction, which this ledger already follows for defeaters: retain a resolved item as commentary rather than deleting it.
attrs.statement: A revision whose transition identity is unsound is marked quarantined with its incident, its reason and its CLASS, keeps its receipt bytes unedited, and may never be an ancestor of the canonical head or become the head. Heredity is a property of the CLASS: a quarantine for invalid transition lineage travels with ancestry; one for a repairable content defect does not.

attrs.evidence: INV-R6.2 placed this mechanism in "whatever plays the role of the station" and shipped a checker instead, on the reasoning that a gate running after both writes have landed is reading the crime scene. The reasoning is right and the conclusion did not follow: `git update-ref <ref> <new-oid> <old-oid>` updates a ref only after verifying it still holds the expected old OID, which is the promotion predicate exactly. scripts/factory-station.mjs is `head` / `open` / `promote --expect` / `verify` over refs/heads/invariant-canonical. INV-R8-RECOVERY was produced in an isolated worktree opened at the canonical head and promoted through the compare-and-swap; MUT-STALE-PARENT-PROMOTION advances the ref underneath a candidate and watches the promotion be refused.
attrs.gap: IT CANNOT BIND A SESSION THAT DOES NOT CALL IT, and nothing at this layer can — the canonical state is the ref, and the shared working directory remains writable by anyone. Measured during this round rather than argued: a third concurrent session rewrote mosaic/embodiment.json in the shared tree at 17:17 on 2026-08-24, twenty minutes after INV-R6.2's receipt was written. `verify --worktree` names the divergence; it does not prevent it. Multi-ref promotion would need git's `update-ref --stdin` transaction mode and one ref does not. MEASURED AGAIN, AND WORSE, AT INV-R8.1: the shared tree does not hold a stray edit, it holds a COMPLETE alternative successor. Two branches from INV-R6 — {INV-R6.1 -> INV-R6.2 -> INV-R7.1} and INV-R8-RECOVERY — each pass every gate they run, and neither is wrong about itself. That is the invariant failing in real time, in the hour after the audit that named it, and it is the sharpest available statement of why local correctness does not compose into an identified global successor. CORRECTED AT INV-R8.2, and the correction is a retraction. INV-R8.1 added the rule `a head may be amended until something consumes it` and used it five times. It is false: a successful compare-and-swap on the canonical ref is itself a publication event, so `not known to be consumed` was standing in for `known not to have been consumed`. FAC-PROMOTION-FINALITY replaces it and INC-R81-PREMATURE-PROMOTION records what it cost.

attrs.evidence: FOUR occurrences of one class, and the fourth landed in the round that shipped this claim. The R4 brief said `60 records` over a 62-record ledger; the R7.2 brief said `21 sustained defeaters` where the gate printed 22; INV-R8.3 said `four files ship` over six declared untrusted captures; and INV-R9 typed `PROVED 15, OPEN 7, DECLARED 6, KNOWN 3, PROVISIONAL 2, REFUTED 2` into FAC-INTEGRATION-READJUDICATE while describing 34 imports — a histogram that sums to 35, because the fifteenth PROVED candidate is the one disposed as already_present. THE MECHANISM IS THREE PARTS AND THEIR SCOPE IS NOW STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. (a) mosaic/derived/brief-facts.json is DERIVED by check-mosaic §13 and the bundle substitutes {{KEY}} from it, refusing a bare integer before a declared noun in a source brief — this covers BRIEFS and the keys someone thought to derive. (b) check-mosaic §7 matches counted phrases in the ledger’s prose — a backstop over a fixed phrase list. (c) INV-R9.2 adds derivation at the point of use for two more surfaces: check-integration §histogram computes every status histogram from the bucket records and refuses one typed into an integration claim’s prose, and check-lineage §8 derives transition scope and refuses a receipt stating its own. NOTHING COVERS PROSE IN GENERAL.
attrs.gap: THE CLAIM AS ORIGINALLY WORDED — `no count of a registry-derivable quantity is typed into prose` — IS FALSIFIED BY ITS OWN ROUND and is not what the mechanism enforces. What is enforced is: brief text through substitution; the ledger prose a fixed phrase list reaches; integration status histograms; receipt transition scope. A count phrased outside those four surfaces passes, and the R9 histogram is the proof — it was in a ledger field, and §7’s phrase list did not contain that shape, because a phrase list contains the drifts someone has already thought of. THE HONEST FORM OF THE RULE IS NEGATIVE — prose should not state a derivable count at all — and deciding whether a sentence states a cardinality is the definitional-subsumption problem this ledger declined to mechanise at INV-R6. A HISTORICAL count must also stay a literal (`R7.1 counted 21 repaired defects` is a fact about a past state), so the lint carries an as-of form, and every count in this evidence field about a PAST artifact is one of those.

attrs.gap: A GRAPH PROPERTY AND NOTHING MORE, and the distance between this and reproducibility is the point of FAC-DERIVATION-CLOSED. It does not give determinism, confluence or evidential force — a single-node registry running `date +%s%N > out.txt` is single-writer, self-read-free and acyclic, and produces different bytes on every run. That counterexample ships as a permanent falsifier.

attrs.gap: A CONTRACT IS A NECESSARY CONDITION, NOT A JUDGEMENT. `rejected` checks that a rejected candidate is not in the ledger as an import; it cannot check that rejecting it was right. `historical_only` checks a revision scope is named; it cannot check the claim is genuinely historical. The one disposition whose contract reaches its meaning is `already_present`, and only because the meaning was relocated into an argument — which is then DECLARED and not discharged (FAC-INTEGRATION-SUBSUMPTION). Second: four of the six dispositions are exercised by zero records in the only integration this tree has, so their contracts are checked by mutation controls rather than by production data. AND ONE CONTRACT TOOK TWO REFUSALS TO GET RIGHT, which is worth recording because both were the same mistake. The file-disposition contract first asked `does this path exist` — and README.md and two captured gate outputs are `build_product_not_content`, ABSENT from the source tree and PRESENT in the extraction, because the extraction is what the build writes them into. Asking the filesystem answered a question about a directory; the disposition is about the canonical set. The second attempt used three states — canonical, narrative, neither — and was refused too, because README.md is declared narrative with commit:false, which is a fact about how THIS lane ships it and not about what the source lane’s delta said it was. What a file disposition can mechanically carry is ONE BIT: is this path canonical source here. The finer distinction is prose in `means`.

What is NOT open is whether the disposition is well-formed: it names a typed relation, an argument, and a pair, and a remapping is refused. What is open is whether the relation holds.

A PRIVILEGE SET A RECORD GRANTS ITSELF IS NOT A CONTRACT. target_local_fields is now the closed triple last_verified / imported_from / readjudicated; TRANSFORM_KINDS declares `forward` (annotates nothing) and `forward_with_historical_evidence_annotation` (annotates exactly `evidence`, for the as-of scoping of a historical count). Both attacks are registered: MUT-TRANSFORM-LOCAL-WIDENED and MUT-TRANSFORM-ANNOTATION-WIDENED, the second using a plausible `why` so the reason field cannot carry the widening either.

attrs.gap: THE VOCABULARY IS SMALL BECAUSE THE INSTANCE IS SMALL. One transform kind beyond plain forwarding, one annotatable field, eight production records. A future integration wanting a different legitimate annotation must add a kind here and a mutation beside it — which is the intended cost, and it is a cost, not a proof that the two kinds are sufficient.

attrs.evidence: Implemented for ONE verifier and declared as policy for the rest. scripts/check-integration.mjs returns 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 NOT_STATED; --report-only never emits a PASS verdict; make-invariant-review-bundle.sh refuses 2 exactly as it refuses 1. THE UNIVERSAL FORM OF THIS CLAIM WAS SHIPPED PROVED AT INV-R9.3 AND WAS FALSE OF THIS ARTIFACT: GPT-5.6 reproduced check-publication-identity.mjs printing `walk is NOT stated` at exit 0 and check-lineage.mjs printing `draft count is NOT stated` at exit 0. Its own gap said so — `one gate has three outcomes and the other fifteen have two` — and a gap paragraph was allowed to narrow a universal statement after the status had been granted. GPT-5.6 also ruled that mechanically converting every gate is the WRONG repair: a checker total over its declared inputs needs no NOT_STATED, and the missing object is a census of which gates are partial over their environment.
attrs.gap: NO CENSUS EXISTS. Until one does, nothing here says which of the sixteen gates OUGHT to be three-valued, so the policy cannot be enforced and is DECLARED for exactly that reason. The exact-scope result is FAC-INTEGRATION-NOT-STATED-NONPASSING and it is the only thing this artifact has PROVED about the subject.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9.2 audit §4. It is the consumer-boundary form of FAC-RESIDUAL-TRUST-UNGATED, which INV-R9.2 opened at the argument boundary: honest disclosure of an unproved premise is not refusal to consume the result.
attrs.review_focus: A census of partial-versus-total gates is the next object. Is `partial over its execution environment` decidable from a gate’s inputs, or does each gate have to declare it?
attrs.statement: FACTORY DESIGN RULE: a required verifier result that is not established may not be consumed as PASS. Where a checker is partial over its execution environment, NOT STATED is a third outcome distinct from PASS and FAIL, and a promotion may consume only PASS.

attrs.evidence: Lineage relies on prior receipt CONTENTS — `invariants.before` is checked against the parent's `after`, and the delta is computed against the parent's manifest — while nothing bound those contents. A parent receipt is writable JSON; editing one after its child was written left every gate green. A child cannot hash itself, but it can hash every parent, which turns the chain into a content-linked history without waiting for signatures. MUT-PARENT-RECEIPT-EDIT alters a parent receipt and leaves the child untouched, and check-lineage §5 refuses.
attrs.gap: This is content-linking, NOT authentication. Nothing signs a receipt, nothing timestamps one, and an editor who changes a parent may simply update the child's recorded digest too — the chain then remains internally consistent and says nothing about who wrote it or when. That is FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH and it is open. The binding is worth having anyway: it makes an isolated edit fail loudly, which is the common case.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §9. Hash chaining, as in a Merkle-linked log; in-toto link chains verified against an intended sequence.
attrs.statement: A child receipt binds the sha256 of its parent receipt's bytes, so the chain of named JSON files is content-linked and a parent edited after its child breaks verification.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's observation, and this loop supplies the data for it. Rounds 3, 4.1 and 5 each closed ZERO table cells; all three added claim-discipline machinery. Under a cells-closed measurand the loop has been stalled for three rounds; under a claims-settled measurand it has not. Both measurands are now written down in mosaic/objectives.json and they are left DISAGREEING, because picking the flattering one is the failure this record exists to name. What is NOT established is any obligation to promote on a cadence: the honest statement is that safe rejection, deadlock, evaluator starvation, permanently unresolved assumptions and productive refusal are five different states and this loop currently cannot tell them apart.
attrs.prior_art: The safety/liveness decomposition (Alpern & Schneider 1985) is the formal neighbourhood; GPT-5.6 supplied the application to a self-improving factory.
attrs.review_focus: Three rounds of zero cells closed is either the discipline paying for itself before the next theorem, or a loop that has found it easier to improve its own bookkeeping than to answer a hard question. Nothing in the artifact distinguishes those, and this record does not either.
attrs.statement: Safety and progress need separate semantics: a factory that refuses every change satisfies every preservation invariant, so 'no invariant was broken' cannot be the definition of a successful round.

attrs.evidence: INV-R8.1 promoted and then force-tagged one revision id through five further canonical commits, on a rule it stated itself: A HEAD MAY BE AMENDED UNTIL SOMETHING CONSUMES IT. GPT-5.6 refuted the premise in a line that generalises — NOT KNOWN TO BE CONSUMED IS NOT KNOWN NOT TO HAVE BEEN CONSUMED. A successful CAS on the canonical ref IS a publication event: any reader anywhere observes the ref the instant it advances, and no consumer registry exists that could establish otherwise. It is the same epistemic substitution this ledger has eliminated at five other layers, made about its own history by the round that built the mechanism. `git tag -f` is removed from scripts/factory-station.mjs; a promotion whose revision id already names a commit is refused BEFORE the ref advances, which is where the first version of this check was not. The selftest creates an id, fails to move it, and then creates a fresh id as the positive control.
attrs.gap: ENFORCED FROM INV-R8.2 AND NOT BEFORE. The six INV-R8.1 commits and their tags stay exactly as they are — retroactive enforcement over immutable history is how you edit the past to satisfy the present — so the artifact permanently contains six canonical commits under one revision id, and INC-R81-PREMATURE-PROMOTION is the record of why. Second: the rule constrains what a station may do to the ref; it does not stop a promotion of an UNFINISHED candidate, which is the actual mistake underneath. `finished` is not a mechanical property and this claim does not pretend to make it one. Third: nothing prevents a session from running `git tag -f` by hand — the refusal is in the station, not in the repository.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/factory-station.mjs — promote (tag created once) and selftest; scripts/check-mosaic.mjs — P.promotionFinality
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R8.1, §4. SLSA Source v1.2: a source revision is a logically immutable snapshot. git-tag(1): use a new tag name once an old one could have been observed, because otherwise two consumers hold different content under one version name.
attrs.statement: Every successful compare-and-swap that advances the canonical ref creates a new immutable source revision. A revision id, once it names a canonical commit, may never be moved. Drafts are amendable; a correction after promotion is a new revision id.

attrs.evidence: INV-R8.2 made promotion final and published across two separate git ref transactions — compare-and-swap the canonical branch, then `git tag` the revision id. GPT-5.6 reproduced the split: with the tag absent at the check, the CAS succeeds, an interleaved writer creates the revision id against another commit, and `git tag` then fails, leaving the canonical branch at the candidate while the revision identity names a stranger. A crash between the two commands leaves the analogous canonical-but-untagged state. Either way the successor is VISIBLE TO EVERY READER before its identity exists, and the refusal fires after the thing it refuses has happened — which is the defect INV-R8.2 corrected one layer up and reintroduced one layer down. Repair: `git update-ref --stdin` in start/prepare/commit form carries `update <ref> <new> <expected-old>` and `create refs/tags/<id> <new>` in a single transaction; git locks every ref at prepare and moves none unless all locks hold. Reproduced in both directions before and after (scripts/factory-station.mjs selftest, MUT-PUBLICATION-TAG-RACE and MUT-PUBLICATION-HEAD-RACE), each paired with the SUPERSEDED two-step sequence on identical inputs as a differential control.
attrs.gap: ATOMIC WITHIN ONE REPOSITORY, WHICH IS THE ONLY PLACE THE CANONICAL STATE LIVES — but git ref transactions are atomic per repository, so a future factory whose canonical state spanned two repositories, or a repository plus an index, would need a protocol this claim does not supply. Second, and unchanged from FAC-CANONICAL-HEAD-CAS: this binds a session that CALLS the station. It cannot bind one that writes the shared directory and never promotes. Third: `create` refuses a revision id that exists, so the id space is the boundary of identity here — two factories sharing a repository and a naming scheme would collide correctly, two using different schemes would not collide at all.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/factory-station.mjs — publish() and the promote path; the differential control is in selftest
attrs.prior_art: git-update-ref(1), transactional mode: refs are locked at `prepare` with their expected values and the transaction aborts rather than partially committing. GPT-5.6 named the primitive in its audit of INV-R8.2. The property is the one SLSA Source v1.2 assumes when it treats a revision as a logically immutable snapshot — a snapshot whose identity is assigned after publication was, for a window, a different object under the same name.
attrs.review_focus: The claim is about a COMPOSITION, not a primitive. INV-R8.2's selftest proved `git update-ref` compares before it swaps and `git tag` refuses to move an existing tag — both true, both still true, and neither able to observe this defect, because the defect was in the order `promote` called them. Is `publish()` now the only path by which either ref moves, and is the differential control the right shape for a repair — running the superseded implementation on identical inputs and asserting it produces the split state?
attrs.statement: Publishing a canonical successor and establishing its immutable revision identity is ONE all-or-none factory operation: either the canonical ref advances AND the revision id is created for that exact commit, or neither ref moves.

attrs.evidence: Fable 5 reconstructed the full promoted revision-name to OID mapping for the post-recovery chain from one read of refs/heads/invariant-canonical, walking parent.commit_oid through committed receipts, and GPT-5.6 independently reproduced it against the shipped INV-R8.3 bundle. scripts/check-publication-identity.mjs re-runs that walk at every head. The reader protocol matters and is part of the claim: git's multi-ref transaction is all-or-none in what it COMMITS, but a concurrent reader may still observe a subset of the changed refs, so a reader that combines a branch read with a tag read can see a mixed snapshot. Under the one-ref protocol subset visibility can stale a convenience index and cannot produce two identities for an OID already read.
attrs.gap: CONTENT-INTEGRITY-BOUND AND SELF-IDENTIFYING FROM THE OID HANDLE — NOT SELF-AUTHENTICATING, and the wrong word was in the Fable witness's own conclusion. A git OID content-binds an object under the hash assumption. It does not establish who produced it, whether the canonical ref was rolled back, whether an attacker replaced the whole repository or bundle, or whether the head is fresh. Those are FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH and remain open. Second, the minimality half is scoped to THIS publication interface: in a pull-based git design exposing a moving current head, one mutable canonical ref suffices for identity discovery — an append-only publication log or out-of-band immutable OID delivery is a counter-design, so the universal form Fable proposed is not claimed. Third: this is a PROTOCOL theorem, not a git theorem, and it binds only readers who follow the protocol.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's adjudication §2 and §3. SLSA Source v1.2 on logically immutable source revisions; git-update-ref(1) on committed-versus-observed ref state.
attrs.review_focus: The claim now rests on a declared observer protocol. Is the protocol stated precisely enough that a reader can tell whether they are following it — and is there anything in this artifact that reads a tag to establish identity?
attrs.statement: From the chain root onward the factory treats the canonical commit OID plus the committed receipt as authoritative source identity: a reader takes ONE ref read, uses the returned OID as an immutable handle, and derives revision identity from committed content without consulting the tag namespace.

assumptions: the substrate executed the check as written (ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY)
attrs.evidence: MEASURED across all 17 receipts. TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS shared the block. COPY: INV-R8.3, INV-R9 and INV-R9.1 each ship lineage.parent_ids [“INV-R8.1-CONCURRENCY-OBSERVED”] beside a `parent` field naming INV-R8.2, INV-R8.3 and INV-R9 respectively — wrong when written, carried forward by copy, and the chain starts at INV-R8.3, one round earlier than the audit that found it located it. Their `rollback_target` is stale by the same route, and INV-R9.1’s reconstruction still owes “INV-R7.1’s content, replayed onto this head” in the receipt of the round that integrated it. SNAPSHOT: four receipts list one unpromoted revision where the registry now holds five — each was CORRECT when written, and a snapshot of mutable state inside an immutable record is not at risk of going stale, it is guaranteed to, and under FAC-PROMOTION-FINALITY it cannot be repaired in place. The same rule reaches scope prose: three receipts say “Nothing else” beside a DERIVED tree_delta of 10, 9 and 8 paths. check-lineage §8 derives all of it, prints it, and from INV-R9.2 refuses a receipt carrying a derivable lineage field or stating its own scope in prose.
attrs.gap: THE PHRASE TEST IS A BACKSTOP AND THE WEAKER HALF, exactly as FAC-COUNT-DERIVED says of §7. Deciding whether a sentence states a scope is the same undecidable problem as deciding whether it states a cardinality; the four patterns matched here are the ones already observed. THE PRIMARY REPAIR IS REMOVAL — INV-R6.2’s ruling when `_round` became a pointer: there is no reason for a second account to exist, and render-and-compare would hide the duplicate rather than remove it. Second: the rule is ENFORCED_FROM INV-R9.2 and the earlier receipts keep their drift, because a new invariant cannot bind immutable history; nine notes print every run and none of them fails. THIRD, AND MEASURED ON THIS ROUND’S OWN RECEIPT: the phrase test cannot distinguish USE from MENTION. The first draft of INV-R9.2’s transition.candidate quoted INV-R9.1’s `Nothing else` in order to name the defect, and the gate refused it — correctly by its own rule and wrongly as a matter of meaning. The quotation moved to transition.why, which is not scanned. That is not a repair; it is where a pattern list stops, and it is the second reason the primary mechanism is REMOVAL of the field rather than matching of its contents.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9 audit §§9–10, which found the stale block on two receipts and the false transition sentence on one.
attrs.review_focus: The SNAPSHOT half generalises past receipts: any immutable record that embeds the current state of a mutable registry has this defect. Does the artifact hold others?
attrs.statement: A transition receipt keeps no second, independently writable account of its own ancestry or of its own scope. Parentage, rollback target, revision states and delta size are derived from the authoritative fields, the registry and the repository, and a receipt written under the rule may not carry them.

attrs.evidence: R5's receipt used 16-hex truncated digests and no signatures — adequate for accidental-drift detection, which is what it was for, and not a provenance boundary. R5.1 moves to full sha256 because that costs nothing; the rest is genuinely open. What is NOT done: no signing, no content-addressed receipt id, no external root of trust, and the evaluator identities in the receipt are strings anyone with write access can type. The word 'immutable' has been removed from the receipt's own description of itself.
attrs.prior_art: in-toto: signed layouts define authorized functionaries, and signed link metadata binds commands, materials and products for later chain verification. SLSA v1.2 Build and Source tracks.
attrs.statement: A receipt that becomes a trust boundary needs full content digests, a content-addressed id, and a signature or an external append-only authority; nothing writable and unsigned may be called immutable in a security sense.

attrs.evidence: R5 already declared its receipt non-decisive and said why. GPT-5.6 sharpened what decisive would mean, and the sharpening matters: today the gate checks that `decision.verdict` is a member of {promote, reject, quarantine, rollback}, which validates the SHAPE of a candidate-supplied answer. In the decisive form the verdict does not appear in the input at all — the function verifies digests and refs, evaluates the hard constraints, applies the selection policy, records which checks ran, and emits verdict and receipt atomically. Then there is no second representation to drift. NOT BUILT, and deliberately not faked: mosaic/receipts/INV-R5.1.json carries honesty.decisive = false.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, round-5 Mosaic audit §9. in-toto's layout + signed link metadata is the mature shape for the provenance half.
attrs.statement: A decisive receipt is the OUTPUT of one admission function — adjudicate(candidate, inputs) -> (verdict, receipt) — not a document written after a gate ran and checked for a well-formed verdict field.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's reproduction against the finished INV-R6.2 artifact. `EMB-CUT-EMPTY` and `EMB-BATTERY-SPLIT` are both PROVED and both rest on scripts/emb-battery-control.mjs. That file appears in no receipt manifest and in no `gates_run`. Modifying it so its final failure exit can never fire, and leaving the receipt untouched, left `check-mosaic`, `check-lineage` and `check-claim-ledger` all exiting 0. A receipt that promotes a claim without binding the bytes of its proof is not describing the evidence state it promoted. THE CLOSURE WALKER IS NOT NEW TO THIS ARTIFACT: make-invariant-review-bundle.sh has computed the transitive import closure of every named witness since round 2.1, when the archive shipped test/laws.mjs beside one of the twelve modules it imports and existsSync reported true the whole time. It was used to decide what to COPY INTO THE ZIP and never to decide what to BIND. scripts/factory-scope.mjs is that same walk pointed at the manifest, and the manifest went from 23 paths to the derived closure.
attrs.gap: DECLARED rather than PROVED, and three gaps are load-bearing. (1) The import walk is STATIC: a dynamic `import()` with a computed specifier is invisible to it, which is DEF-REPRO-DYNAMIC-IMPORT and no witness in the tree uses one. (2) Closure covers what the registries REFERENCE; a proof that lives only in a human's head, or in an evidence file no record names, is outside it by construction. (3) The `scripts/`, `AmpersandBoxDesign/` and `opensentience.org/` roots are closure-only rather than walk-closed, because those directories are shared with other lanes in the source tree; a factory file that no derivation reaches is caught only by the git-tree mode, which needs the repository.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §7. in-toto: a step records its exact materials and products, and verification checks the links against the layout — provenance is a relation between an exact step, exact inputs and exact outputs.
attrs.statement: A transition receipt binds the transitive evidence closure of every settled claim and decision it promotes — witnesses, argument evidence, instrument implementations, incident reproducers, and the relative-import closure of every executable among them — not only the registries and gates the transition itself invoked.

attrs.evidence: True as stated at INV-R6.2 and too weak to be worth stating alone, which is why it is superseded rather than repaired. GPT-5.6 measured the implementation against its own prose twice. (1) The prose said the canonical set was `every mosaic/**.json`; the code enumerated `mosaic/*.json` + `mosaic/derived/*.json`, so `mosaic/newdir/new-registry.json` could be added to the finished artifact with the Mosaic gate still exiting 0 — the declared scope and the implemented scope were different sets and nothing compared them. (2) The larger hole: registries and gates are not the only bytes a transition promotes. `scripts/emb-battery-control.mjs` is the load-bearing evidence under two SETTLED claims and is neither a registry nor a gate, so it entered no manifest; a copy of the finished artifact with its final failure exit made unreachable passed check-mosaic, check-lineage and check-claim-ledger together.
attrs.gap: SUPERSEDED at INV-R8-RECOVERY by FAC-RECEIPT-EVIDENCE-CLOSED. Registry-and-gate coverage is a proper subset of evidence closure and the difference is exactly where the exploit lived. The record is kept, not deleted: it names the scope this artifact thought was sufficient for one round.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/check-mosaic.mjs — P.receiptScopeClosed, and the derived canonical set in scripts/receipt-digests.mjs
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.1. The reference-monitor criterion `always invoked`, applied to a manifest rather than to a check.
attrs.statement: Every canonical REGISTRY and GATE participating in a transition is bound by that transition's receipt, or is excluded by naming another transition that has a receipt.

attrs.evidence: Both alternatives were tried in argument and refused. INV-R6.2 refused to rewrite the tree so that INV-R6.1 contained no R7 material, because that means deleting a concurrent agent's round and re-authoring it from the migration scripts of the party whose collision caused the problem — a receipt describing a transition no session performed. That refusal was right. What did not follow is that the mixed branch should stay canonical HEAD: those are not the only two options. INV-R8-RECOVERY starts from the INV-R6 commit in an isolated worktree, replays the reviewed content of INV-R6.1, the concurrent INV-R7 and INV-R6.2, and is promoted as a single child of INV-R6 under a revision id no quarantined receipt uses. The damaged branch is preserved unedited on refs/heads/invariant-quarantine. No fabricated intermediate transition is required, and the history says one true thing where it used to say two contradictory ones.
attrs.gap: The replay was performed and reviewed BY THE SAME EVALUATOR that implemented the round — mosaic/objectives.json §exteriority, unsatisfied for a fifth consecutive round. What makes this weaker than a clean history rather than equal to one: `INV-R8-RECOVERY.tree_delta` is derived from bytes and is exact, but WHICH of the mixed branch's changes were intended is a judgement, and the brief carries it in prose. The reviewed-versus-replayed correspondence is checkable only by reading ROUND8_RECOVERY_BRIEF.md against the quarantined artifact.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §11. The version-control distinction between `revert` (a new commit that undoes) and `reset --hard` (a history that no longer contains the mistake).
attrs.statement: A damaged lineage is repaired by ONE new transition from the last verified-good ancestor that replays the reviewed content of the damaged branch under a fresh revision id — not by rewriting the damaged receipts and not by continuing from them.

attrs.evidence: INV-R9 named every hole INV-R9.2 closes, in three separate structured fields, and shipped the claim PROVED beside all three. ARG-INTEGRATION-DIFF-COVERAGE.remaining_trust: “That candidate_count itself is the true size of the delta — it is written by the generator from the pinned artifacts and is NOT recomputed at gate time.” FAC-INTEGRATION-REVIEWED-DIFF.gap: “the file buckets are asserted by the generator rather than checked.” The manifest’s own _comment: “Every count in this file is computed by scripts/gen-manifest” — naming a path that is not in the tree and never was. Each is exactly the premise a later mutation exploited. MEASURED across the ledger: 3 of 19 arguments declare remaining trust in the language of not-checked, all three on PROVED claims; the other two are residuals genuinely outside the artifact’s reach (a computed dynamic import that no witness uses; a domain-extension re-run) and were not exploitable. So the pattern is real and rare, and one of three was load-bearing.
attrs.gap: THE RULE AS STATED IS NOT MECHANISABLE — deciding whether a residual premise is one the conclusion quantifies over is the definitional-subsumption problem again. The DECIDABLE SHADOW, in the sense INV-R7.3 used for non-bypassability, is a phrase test over `remaining_trust` on arguments concluding settled claims, and it is REPORTED by check-claim-ledger rather than gated: a rule that reads as enforced while catching only the phrasings someone thought of is worse than an open claim (H8-SERIALIZABLE-PROMOTION, INV-R8). This is the round’s open question and it is put to the adjudicator rather than answered here.
attrs.prior_art: INV-R8.2 established the special case: SELF-DOUBT IN A COVERING LETTER IS NOT A REFUSAL — a suspect rule flagged in its own handoff and shipped anyway. This generalises it from the covering letter to the ledger’s own structured honesty fields: a `gap` is not a gate.
attrs.review_focus: Is there a form of this rule that binds without becoming a phrase list? The candidate shape is that a coverage argument’s remaining_trust must name only premises OUTSIDE the conclusion’s quantification domain, which needs the domain to be a machine object rather than a sentence.
attrs.statement: A claim may not be PROVED while an argument leg supporting it declares, in `remaining_trust`, that a premise its own conclusion quantifies over is not checked. The honesty fields of this ledger record residual trust; they do not discharge it, and nothing currently stops a disclosure from standing in for a refusal.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's record, adopted as open. The distinction is already PROVED one level down: LED-C9-MEDIATED for the absorbing sink, LED-NARROW for the half that is NOT forbidden (allocating unspent budget remains feasible; only recovering spent value is refused). What is missing is the lift from resources to operations. A source edit is reversible by git; a migration is often only compensatable; publishing a secret is irreversible; training a descendant on an artifact may be harder to revoke than deleting the artifact.
attrs.prior_art: The affine ledger's reversible/irreversible split (in-tree). Externally, reversibility taxonomies for agent actions distinguish instantly reversible, multi-step reversible, and irreversible-without-external-intervention, and note that time sensitivity is a separate axis — cited for the shape of the vocabulary, not for a threshold.
attrs.statement: Every factory operation declares whether its semantic effects are reversible, compensatable or irreversible, and promotion policy holds irreversible effects to a stricter evidence and authority threshold.

attrs.evidence: The round's result, and it is about the factory rather than the product. INV-R6.1 and a concurrent INV-R7 Embodiment round were written into one working tree at the same time, both branching from INV-R6. The R6.1 receipt then claimed ONE parent and ONE operation over a state containing two, and disclosed the ambiguity in prose. That disclosure was honest and insufficient: a transition receipt exists to identify an exact parent, an exact operation and an exact successor, and one that cannot is byte-consistent with a history that did not happen. This is the C10 shape at transition scope — two descriptions of what happened, diverging. The discipline is database serializability applied to recursive self-improvement: read parent P, work against an isolated snapshot of P, verify canonical HEAD is still P before promoting, and on drift abort, rebase, or record an explicit two-parent merge. LOCALLY VALID CONCURRENT IMPROVEMENTS DO NOT AUTOMATICALLY COMPOSE INTO AN HONESTLY IDENTIFIED GLOBAL SUCCESSOR. AT INV-R8-RECOVERY: the counterexample is preserved rather than repaired. INV-R6.1 and INV-R6.2 keep their bytes and are QUARANTINED — never an ancestor of the canonical head — and the canonical head is one recovery_replay whose single parent is the verified INV-R6. Preserving bad history does not require continuing to build on it.
attrs.gap: THE ENFORCEMENT HALF NOW EXISTS AND HAS BEEN USED EXACTLY ONCE. scripts/factory-station.mjs opens an isolated worktree at the canonical head, and promotes with `git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`, which advances the ref only if it still holds the expected parent OID. INV-R8-RECOVERY is the first round promoted through it. WHAT IS STILL NOT TRUE: the station cannot bind a session that never calls it. The canonical state is the REF, not the shared directory, and a session writing the directory is not promoting anything — but it is also not refused. Measured during this round: at 17:17 on 2026-08-24 a third concurrent session rewrote mosaic/embodiment.json in the shared tree with no transition at all, and the head receipt's digest for that path stopped reproducing. `factory-station.mjs verify --worktree` reports such a divergence in one line; it does not prevent it. The claim also remains DECLARED because one promotion is not "every promoted round".
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/factory-station.mjs — the compare-and-swap; scripts/check-lineage.mjs — the shape
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.1. Database serializability and optimistic concurrency control; the compare-and-swap discipline of a distributed version-control push.
attrs.statement: Every promoted round is derivable from the exact parent receipt it names; a canonical child may not silently contain edits from an unrecorded sibling branch.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's record, adopted as open, and the reason it matters is that it removes a false prerequisite: a factory does not have to prove an experimental component correct before the component may ever be useful. It has to contain it. The prior art is mature and was verified this round rather than accepted on citation.

assumptions: D finite
Γ a finite set of finitary relations on D
attrs.evidence: Derived from standard finite-CSP algebra: every finite structure has a core (Hell–Nešetřil 1992); endomorphisms preserve pp-definable relations; the canonical conjunctive query at an element of a finite core pp-defines its automorphism orbit. (⇐) transitivity makes every non-empty pp-definable unary relation contain the whole core. (⇒) two orbits give two disjoint non-empty pp-definable unary relations. Checked on nine languages against the symmetry certificate and the bounded search, with no disagreement on any conclusive result.
attrs.prior_art: Ingredients standard — Hell–Nešetřil 1992 (cores); Bodirsky, Graph Homomorphisms and Universal Algebra Prop. 5.10 (pp-definable orbits); Jeavons–Cohen–Gyssens 1997 (Inv–Pol). NOVELTY OF THE EQUIVALENCE IS NOT CLAIMED and no exact prior-art search has been done: publish it as "the constraint template has a transitive core", derived here, not as a named classical theorem.
attrs.review_focus: The equivalence is short and its ingredients are textbook, which is exactly the profile of a result someone has already published. FED-1PA-NAME is the search, and it is still open.
attrs.statement: Γ has the one-variable gluing property (working-1PA) if and only if the automorphism group of the core of (D; Γ) acts transitively on the core.

assumptions: |D|^|D| endomorphism enumeration is affordable — the implementation refuses above a declared bound rather than hanging
attrs.evidence: decide1PA enumerates End(A), takes a minimum-image endomorphism f, builds the genuine retraction r = p⁻¹∘f (p = f restricted to the image, a bijection because minimality forces f(B) = B), and tests transitivity of Aut(B) over permutations of B. The retraction is checked to be idempotent, identity on the core, and an endomorphism. refute1PA builds the two-site canonical-query federation; on every failing language it has both sites satisfiable, exactly one shared variable, κ_splitBerge = 0, and an unsatisfiable union.
attrs.prior_art: The procedure follows from FED-1PA-DEC being KNOWN; what is claimed here is that it runs and agrees. REPEATED SQUARING IS NOT A CORE RETRACTION — iterating f^(2^k) never reaches an idempotent for a permutation of order 3 — and the round-3 research implementation returned a map under that name that was not one. GPT-5.6, round-3 audit.
attrs.statement: The exact decision procedure for the transitive-core property is implemented here and is conclusive in both directions, returning a running refutation when the property fails.

attrs.evidence: None. The sharp question is whether the language can pp-define TWO DISJOINT non-empty unary projections — equivalently, whether ⋂U_Γ is empty (FED-1PA-HELLY). ROUND 3 sharpened what has to be specified before this can be decided at all: sorts, a domain model per sort, relation symbols with sorted scopes, which literals/constants are admitted as atoms, and which schema-level universal constraints (keys, mandatory participation, uniqueness) lie OUTSIDE the instance-CSP model. The multi-sorted theorem is available — the property holds at separator sort σ iff Aut(core) is transitive on the σ-part — but the CORE IS GLOBAL to the multi-sorted structure and is not obtained by solving each sort independently. Indicative reading of representative fragments: identity sorts with =/≠ pass; a value sort passes until it carries two literals, and then fails. That makes 36b, not 36a, the likely route for real value sorts.
attrs.gap: This is the load-bearing open question under cell 36 and the reason its status is `conditional` rather than `proved`.
attrs.review_focus: No FGAP language exists in a form precise enough to decide this. Representative Neo4j/GQL-like fragments are examples, not the user's language, and classifying them settles nothing about FGAP.
attrs.statement: The constraint languages a real federated property graph would carry have 1PA.
attrs.supersedes: Round 2 asserted that 'if any federated relation can pin a variable to a value, 1PA fails outright'. THAT IS FALSE, and it was the sentence the practical question was built on. Over D = {0,1} a language whose only pin is x = 0 realizes projections {0} and {0,1}, which intersect — so it pins a value AND has 1PA. Failure needs two DISJOINT projections, e.g. pp-defining both {0} and {1}. Both cases are now checked in §4. Correction from GPT-5.6's round-2 audit.

assumptions: Finite domain. The executable corroboration runs over a BOUNDED subfamily of U_Γ (instances of ≤3 constraints, ≤2 auxiliary variables), so it corroborates the equivalence rather than deciding 1PA for a language.
attrs.evidence: (⟸) a common element makes every pair intersect. (⟹) under 1PA, U_Γ is closed under non-empty intersection: given U, V realized by I₁, I₂, rename auxiliary variables apart and identify only x; the union is satisfiable by 1PA and its projection at x is exactly U ∩ V. D is finite, so U_Γ is finite, so ⋂U_Γ is a finite intersection of members and is itself a member — hence non-empty. ∎ Checked on six languages including the two that fail: pairwise-intersecting ⟺ a common element exists, 0 mismatches, and closure under intersection holds wherever 1PA does. ROUND 3: this is a corollary of the transitive-core theorem and NOT a prior-art search key. Closure of U_Γ under intersection holds for every Γ — pp-definable relations are closed under conjunction — so the "Helly" content is a fact about pp-definability, not a property of the language. It remains true and remains a useful reformulation; it is just not the thing to look up.
attrs.gap: This form is simpler than the pairwise one and may yield both a decision procedure and the established name. Contributed by GPT-5.6 in the round-2 audit.
attrs.prior_art: NOT SEARCHED, and this is the highest-value prior-art target in the round. 'Every pair intersects ⟹ the whole family intersects' is a HELLY property; Helly properties of constraint languages, unary pp-definable relations under Inv–Pol, and variable-elimination properties are the neighbourhoods to search. Novelty is not claimed.
attrs.statement: Γ has 1PA ⟺ the intersection of ALL non-empty unary pp-definable projections of Γ is non-empty — i.e. some single domain value belongs to every member of U_Γ = { π_x(sol I) : I a satisfiable Γ-instance }.

assumptions: D finite
the core of (D; Γ) is automorphism-transitive
attrs.evidence: ⋂U_Γ is pp-definable, contains B, and is End-invariant, so it contains every h(B); conversely it is contained in the member End(A)·b. Checked by requiring every bounded realized projection to contain the computed hull, on every language of the §4b table where the property holds.
attrs.prior_art: Corollary of FED-1PA-CORE.
attrs.statement: When Γ has a transitive core B, the intersection of all non-empty unary pp-definable relations of Γ equals End(A)·b for any b in B — the endomorphic hull of the core.

attrs.evidence: Successor on a 6-path over |D| = 6 fails the property — its core is all of D with six singleton orbits — and find1PAViolation reports null at its default bounds. The witness appears only at maxAux 3. The bounded search remains a sound FALSIFIER: a hit exhibits its witness. It was never a decision procedure and this is the construction that says so. TIMELESS because the bounds are named in the statement: raising the defaults does not make a miss AT THESE BOUNDS conclusive, it produces a different proposition. R4.1 REMOVED AN OVERREACH HERE. R3.1 appended "FED-WITNESS-BOUND makes the minimum grow with Σ|R^A|, so no fixed bound is ever conclusive" — which is an upper bound on the minimum used as a lower one, and is false (FED-MIN-GROWS). The universal statement it was reaching for is now open as FED-1PA-NO-FIXED-BOUND, unsupported.
attrs.prior_art: Fable 5, round-3 research pass.
attrs.statement: A MISS from find1PAViolation at its default bounds (maxCon 3, maxAux 2) is evidence that Γ has the gluing property.

attrs.evidence: Round 3 eliminated three candidates without finding the answer. "1-point amalgamation" collides with the Fraïssé-theoretic one-point amalgamation property and is retired as a public name. "Patchwork" (Lutz–Miličić; Dabrowski et al. AAAI 2021) is a DIFFERENT property — it quantifies over complete satisfiable JEPD networks agreeing on their whole overlap, hypotheses the general finite-template condition does not carry — though the exact relationship in that restricted setting is not settled, and calling the two incomparable outright would overstate it. The common-intersection form is NOT the search key it was proposed as: the closure step needs no hypothesis on Γ at all, so the "Helly property" there is a triviality of pp-closure rather than a property of the language. The nearest classical analogue found is Huang 2012's canonical-solution characterization of patchwork, of which the transitive core is the single-variable case. Until an exact citation exists, publish the descriptive phrase "the constraint template has a transitive core" and claim no name.
attrs.gap: Do not publish `1PA` as settled terminology. Establishing the exact existing name — best attacked via the FED-1PA-HELLY common-intersection form — is the first objective of the next research pass.
attrs.prior_art: Fraïssé amalgamation (collision) · Dabrowski–Jonsson–Ordyniak–Osipov AAAI 2021 (patchwork) · Huang 2012 (canonical solutions) · Bodirsky, Graph Homomorphisms and Universal Algebra (cores, pp-definable orbits). ROUND-4 AUDIT ADDED A UNIVERSAL-ALGEBRA SEARCH FORMULATION, which is a better key than the two already eliminated: for a finite core, transitivity of Aut is equivalent to the polymorphism algebra having NO PROPER NON-EMPTY SUBUNIVERSES. (⟸) each automorphism orbit of a finite core is pp-definable and hence a unary subuniverse, so two orbits give a proper one. (⟹) transitivity leaves no proper invariant subset. Literature on finite transitive cores uses the "no proper subalgebras" consequence explicitly, so that phrase — not "canonical value" and not pp-definable unary relations — is where to search next.
attrs.review_focus: An exact prior-art search for the EQUIVALENCE ITSELF has still not been done. Two search framings are now eliminated and a third (no proper subuniverses) is untried. If it is already published, FED-1PA-CORE should be KNOWN and not PROVED.
attrs.statement: '1-point amalgamation' is the correct name for this property.

attrs.evidence: NOT PROVED, and R3.1 asserted it. It is plausible — probably true — and the only argument offered for it was invalid: FED-WITNESS-BOUND bounds the canonical construction from above and says nothing about how small a refutation can be, which FED-MIN-GROWS makes concrete. Establishing it needs a LOWER-bound family: languages whose MINIMUM refutation size diverges. Note the shape of what is required — not a language with a large canonical query, which is easy, but one where no small refutation exists at all, which is the hard direction and the reason this is a research question rather than a measurement.

attrs.review_focus: This is the load-bearing proposition behind "a bounded search can never decide the property", and nothing here establishes it. Any future claim that a bounded search is inconclusive IN GENERAL must cite this record, and this record is open.
attrs.statement: For every fixed search bound B there is a finite Γ that fails the gluing property but whose every refutation exceeds B.

attrs.evidence: Solution sets of Γ-instances are H-invariant. If I₁, I₂ share only x with solutions α₁, α₂, pick h with h(α₁(x)) = α₂(x); then h∘α₁ ∪ α₂ solves the union. eq/neq is Sym(D)-invariant at every |D|.
attrs.prior_art: Elementary. The polymorphism framing is Jeavons–Cohen–Gyssens 1997.
attrs.statement: If a transitive subgroup of Sym(D) preserves every relation of Γ, then Γ has 1-point amalgamation. (Lemma 3.)

attrs.evidence: Γ = {R} with R = {(0,1),(1,0),(2,1),(1,2)} over |D| = 3. Aut(D; R) fixes 1 (the only degree-2 element) so it is not transitive and the certificate fails, but the retraction 2 ↦ 0 gives the core {0,1} on which Aut acts transitively — so the property HOLDS. Value symmetry is strictly stronger than the real condition, which is what makes FED-1PA-SYM a certificate rather than a characterization.
attrs.prior_art: Fable 5, round-3 research pass.
attrs.statement: Value symmetry — a transitive subgroup of Sym(D) preserving every relation of Γ — is NECESSARY for the gluing property.

attrs.evidence: (⟸) a split cycle is 2-connected, hence contained in one block, which then carries ≥2 sites. (⟹) any two edges of a block lie on a common cycle, so a block with two sites yields a split cycle. Checked against brute-force enumeration of every simple cycle (including 2-cycles from parallel edges) on 117,648 federations: 0 mismatches.
attrs.prior_art: Block decomposition: Whitney 1932; Diestel Graph Theory §3.1.
attrs.statement: κₛ(G, site) := Σ over blocks B of max(0, |sites(B)| − 1) is zero exactly when no cycle of the carrier is split across sites.

attrs.evidence: Matroid components are the classes of "lie on a common circuit" (Oxley §4.1); for the cycle matroid of a loopless graph the circuits are the cycles and the components are the block edge sets; a separator is a union of components (§4.2) and a partition into separators is a direct-sum decomposition. Verified against κₛ on 117,648 binary federations and on 4,096 n-ary federations, zero mismatches on all three equivalences. This unifies the carriers: for binary constraints the incidence graph is the subdivision of the constraint multigraph, so ONE carrier now covers every arity and the two-carrier machinery retires.
attrs.prior_art: Oxley, Matroid Theory §4.1–4.2 (components, separators, direct sums) — a KNOWN TRANSLATION of a standard matroid fact, not a new theorem. Whitney 1932 for blocks.
attrs.statement: κₛ = 0 if and only if every site's incidence-edge set is a separator of the cycle matroid of the incidence graph — equivalently the site colouring is constant on every matroid component, equivalently the matroid is the direct sum of its site restrictions.

assumptions: "canonical" is not formalized anywhere in this work, which is why this is DECLARED and not open to refutation as stated
attrs.evidence: NOT DERIVED, and round 3 did not refute it either. Five natural magnitudes — impure-component count; Σ max(0, |sites(B)| − 1); minimum recolourings; minimum carrier deletions to purify; and the partition-lattice gap |sites| − #components of the site-conflict graph (the minimum number of site merges, and the only one with a matroid meaning) — are pairwise distinct, all ten pairs separated by explicit federations. That shows the theorem FIXES no magnitude; it does not show none is canonical, because "canonical" has not been defined. The research pass filed this as "canonical magnitude REFUTED"; that is a polarity and formalization error and is not adopted. Sharper evidence against all five: the zero set agrees between the binary constraint multigraph and its incidence-graph subdivision while the magnitudes do not — minimum recolouring reads 2 on a three-site triangle and 4 on its subdivision. THE CLASS IS NAMED DELIBERATELY: what is proved is invariance under THAT ONE normalization, not under some unspecified family of carrier transformations, and "carrier-invariant" should not be published as a general phrase until such a class is defined.
attrs.review_focus: A declared index is the kind of thing that gets cited as if it were derived. If a magnitude is wanted, the first job is to say what "canonical" would mean — invariance under which operations? — and the carrier-invariance failure is the sharpest available test.
attrs.statement: The MAGNITUDE of κₛ is a canonical invariant.

attrs.evidence: Six explicit federations separate all ten pairs. The round-3 research witness printed "magnitudes shown pairwise distinct" while its code compared six hand-listed pairs out of ten, and on its five examples the impure-component count and the minimum-purifying-deletion count are NEVER different. GPT-5.6 caught it and proposed the missing witness: K₄ with one site on a perfect matching has ONE impure component (K₄ is 2-connected, so one block) and needs TWO deletions, because K₄ minus any single edge is still 2-connected and still mixed. That witness is added and all ten pairs are now compared programmatically rather than listed.
attrs.prior_art: Fable 5 (the five magnitudes) · GPT-5.6 (the K₄ separator and the incomplete-pair-list finding).
attrs.statement: The five candidate κₛ magnitudes are pairwise distinct: for each of the ten unordered pairs there is a federation on which they differ.

attrs.evidence: b₁ cannot see the site colouring, and the colouring is the whole content. A single site holding a triangle has b₁ = 1 and NO split cycle, so b₁ reports an obstruction the federation theorem says is absent. b₁ = 0 and κₛ = 0 disagree on 1,440 of the 15,624 four-variable federations.

attrs.statement: Ordinary undirected cycle rank b₁ = |E| − |V| + c is the right replacement for κ as cell 36's carrier.

attrs.evidence: κ is defined on DIRECTED graphs via the largest SCC. Constraint edges are symmetric, so every orientation is arbitrary. CE-D: sites {a≠b, b≠d} and {a=c, c≠d}, oriented a→b, a→c, b→d, c→d — all SCCs trivial, κ = 0, and fidelity fails on the undirected split 4-cycle underneath.

attrs.evidence: Take the pins p₀, p₁ over |D| = 2 — whose refutation p₀(x) | p₁(x) is TWO constraints — and adjoin an irrelevant full k-ary relation. Every map preserves a full relation, so End(A) and the core are unchanged and the language still fails the property; but Σ|R^A| gains 2^k. Measured against the shipped kernel: k=1 gives Σ = 4 and a canonical construction of 8; k=4 gives 18 and 36; k=8 gives 258 and 516 — and at every k the two-constraint witness is still there, with both sites satisfiable, κ_splitBerge = 0 and an unsatisfiable union. AN UPPER BOUND ON THE MINIMUM BOUNDS NOTHING FROM BELOW. This record exists because R3.1 asserted the proposition above while citing FED-WITNESS-BOUND, which establishes the opposite direction; the family is pinned rather than the sentence merely deleted.

assumptions: Cited, not implemented here.

attrs.statement: If sites certify PAIRWISE CONSISTENCY of their solution projections rather than only local satisfiability, the carrier is α-acyclicity of the SITE hypergraph.

attrs.evidence: Four constructions. CE-A kills it on a TREE (site 1 pins v=0, site 2 pins v=1; the carrier is the path a–v–b, so there is no cycle to split) — cyclicity is therefore not the obstruction at all for a general language. CE-B does it at |D|=2 with every relation having full projections, refuting the natural 'arc-consistent language' repair. CE-C repeats the shape at |D|=3 with Z₃ sums.
attrs.finding: REFUTED. The implication fails for general finite constraint languages; the counterexample is exhibited by the gate.
