attrs.statement: For general finite constraint languages, no cycle of the union carrier being split across sites ⟹ fidelity.
attrs.supersedes: INV-R1's evidence line '4 domains, 240k trials, 0 counterexamples', which was evidence for nothing beyond eq/neq: every domain sampled the same value-symmetric language, for which the lemma is a short theorem. The sweep was measuring a theorem, not probing a conjecture.

assumptions: Γ has 1-point amalgamation (1PA): any two satisfiable Γ-instances sharing exactly one variable have a satisfiable union.
attrs.evidence: Block–cut induction. No split cycle ⟺ every block with ≥2 edges is monochromatic (Whitney: any two edges of a 2-connected graph lie on a common cycle), so each block is a sub-multiset of one satisfiable site. Blocks and cut vertices form a TREE; a leaf block meets the rest in exactly one variable; 1PA glues. Corroborated exhaustively: 0 violations over every no-split-cycle federation in a complete 4-variable enumeration at |D|=2 and |D|=3.
attrs.prior_art: PROVED HERE by block–cut induction. Beeri–Fagin–Maier–Yannakakis 1983 is the neighbouring classical result (pairwise ⟹ global consistency on α-acyclic schemes) and the block hypergraph is α-acyclic, but BFMY's pairwise consistency is STRICTLY STRONGER than 1PA's intersecting-projections condition, so this is not a restatement of it. Novelty is NOT claimed — an exact prior-art search has not been done. Explicitly NOT Freuder 1982, which assumes arc consistency of the whole network; CE-A satisfies this cell's antecedent and violates Freuder's.
attrs.statement: If Γ has 1-point amalgamation and no cycle of the union carrier is split across sites, then fidelity holds.

attrs.evidence: (⇐) is FED-Q1-STAR. (⇒) is a construction, and it runs: given two satisfiable instances meeting at one variable with disjoint projections there, make each its own site. They meet at a cut vertex, so no cycle is split; both sites are satisfiable; the union is not. The check finds such a pair for {OR, NAND} at |D|=2 and verifies all four properties of the resulting federation.
attrs.prior_art: As FED-Q1-STAR. Labelled proved-here; not attributed to BFMY.
attrs.statement: Split-cycle sufficiency holds for EVERY Γ-federation if and only if Γ has 1-point amalgamation.

assumptions: the existence of graphs with girth > s and chromatic number > k is Erdős 1959, cited and NOT re-derived here
the executable instance is s = 3, k = 3 only; larger s rests on the citation
attrs.evidence: Take G with girth > s and χ(G) > k. All-≠ on G with one site per edge: every site satisfiable, the union not k-colourable, fidelity fails. Any sub-federation of ≤ s constraints has ≤ s edges and girth > s, so it is a forest, 2-colourable, and has fidelity — soundness fails. Instantiated executably with the Grötzsch graph (11 vertices, 20 edges, girth 4, χ = 4): all 1,140 three-constraint sub-federations have fidelity while the whole does not. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT — for k ≥ 3 a fidelity failure can be irreducibly GLOBAL, carried by no bounded piece of the federation.

every site is locally satisfiable — WITHOUT this the ⟸ direction is false
attrs.evidence: Harary 1953: a signed graph is balanced iff every cycle carries an even number of negative edges, iff its vertices 2-colour. Exhaustive over 117,648 federations: 0 mismatches. The literal conjecture, stated without the antecedent, fails on 15,744 of them — an unbalanced split cycle sitting beside a locally unsatisfiable site makes fidelity vacuously true.
attrs.prior_art: Harary 1953 (balance).
attrs.statement: At |D| = 2 over eq/neq, under the antecedent that every site is satisfiable, fidelity fails if and only if some split cycle is unbalanced in Harary's signed-graph sense (an odd number of ≠ edges).

assumptions: The quantifier class is exactly as defined: P sees the cycle's own labels and site tags and nothing else. A criterion permitted to inspect the rest of the federation, or several cycles jointly, is NOT covered and is a different question.
attrs.evidence: Suppose P is sound and complete. Let F be K₄ all-≠ in three matchings; ¬fidelity(F), so by completeness some cycle C of F satisfies P. Let F' be the federation whose constraints are exactly C's edges with the same relations and site tags. C is a cycle of F', so FAIL_P(F') holds. But F' is a single ≠-cycle: 3-colourable, with every site a sub-multiset of a matching, so fidelity(F') HOLDS — contradicting soundness. ∎ The load-bearing step is checked: all 7 of K₄'s simple cycles keep fidelity when extracted. The |D|=2 contrast is checked too — an unbalanced split cycle STILL fails fidelity when extracted, which is exactly why 'split and unbalanced' is a valid cycle-local criterion there.
attrs.prior_art: Not searched. The statement is elementary once the quantifier class is fixed; the point of fixing it is that the previous informal version could not be attacked.
attrs.review_focus: Proved ONLY for the quantifier class it names. A criterion permitted to inspect several cycles jointly, or the rest of the federation, is untouched — and that is a strictly larger and more interesting class.
attrs.statement: Define a CYCLE-LOCAL CRITERION as a predicate P on (labels(C), sites(C)) — the relations and site tags along a cycle, in order, and nothing else about the federation containing it — inducing the test FAIL_P(F) := ∃ a cycle C of F with P(labels(C), sites(C)). Then at |D| = 3 over {=, ≠} there is NO cycle-local criterion P that is both sound and complete, i.e. satisfies FAIL_P(F) ⟺ ¬fidelity(F) for every federation F.
attrs.superseded_by: FED-Q2-DK-LOCALITY (all k ≥ 3) and FED-Q2-BOUNDED-LOCALITY (all bounded sizes s)

attrs.evidence: χ(K₄) = 4 > 3, so the union has no model. Each site is a perfect matching and trivially satisfiable. Each of the 7 simple cycles is a 3- or 4-cycle of disequalities, and every cycle of ≠ is 2- or 3-colourable. All three facts are computed, not asserted.
attrs.prior_art: The colouring reduction is standard; Erdős 1959 (high girth, high chromatic number) generalizes the construction to arbitrarily large girth.
attrs.statement: At |D| = 3 over {=, ≠}, a fidelity failure need not have any individually unsatisfiable cycle: K₄ with all-≠ edges split into three perfect matchings has every site satisfiable, every simple cycle satisfiable, and no 3-colouring.

The polarity was backwards and 'cycle-local' was never defined. Split into this witness and FED-Q2-D3-LOCALITY.

attrs.evidence: K_{k+1} of all-≠ with one site per edge: every site is a single constraint and so satisfiable, χ(K_{k+1}) = k+1 > k so the union is not, and fidelity fails. Completeness forces P on some cycle; every simple cycle of a complete graph is 2- or 3-colourable and so k-colourable, hence has fidelity when extracted with its own labels and sites, and soundness fails. Executed at k = 3, 4, 5 — 7, 37 and 197 simple cycles respectively, every one keeping fidelity under extraction.

attrs.statement: For EVERY k ≥ 3, over {=, ≠} on |D| = k, no cycle-local criterion is both sound and complete for fidelity failure.

attrs.evidence: H = {a,b,c},{a,b} with site 1 holding the Sym(D)-invariant ternary 'a = b' and site 2 holding a ≠ b. GYO reduces it (α-acyclic); every sub-hypergraph is α-acyclic (β-acyclic); two edges cannot form a γ-cycle. It is Berge-cyclic, both sites are satisfiable, and the union is not. Sampling agrees: α-acyclic unions violate fidelity thousands of times per run.
attrs.prior_art: Fagin 1983 states the mechanism — two hyperedges sharing ≥2 vertices are already Berge-cyclic, which is exactly why database theory weakened the notion. For a local-satisfiability certificate that weakening is unaffordable.

assumptions: Γ has a transitive core (FED-1PA-CORE) — the hypothesis is load-bearing: the {OR, NAND} control violates the conclusion on the same carrier shape
CONSTRAINTS ARE HYPEREDGE INSTANCES, not scopes — see FED-Q3-INSTANCE
attrs.evidence: Proof: no split Berge cycle ⟺ every block of I(H) is site-monochromatic (any two constraint-nodes of a 2-connected block share a cycle); super-blocks (blocks merged across shared constraint-nodes) are then monochromatic and form a tree whose adjacent members share exactly one variable; a leaf glues by the language hypothesis; induct. CORROBORATION IS NOW EXHAUSTIVE, NOT SAMPLED — the previous 20,000-draw sweep is gone. Four complete small spaces over three languages whose hypothesis is CHECKED rather than labelled (Sym(3)-invariant; {U₀, ≤, =} with a singleton core and a genuine unary relation; {≠∘f, R∘R} with a transitive core and no value symmetry), each federation checked three ways — κ_splitBerge against brute-force incidence-cycle enumeration, super-blocks against an independent subset enumeration of hypergraph vertex-articulation blocks, and the theorem against a full satisfiability solve. Zero mismatches, zero violations. The {OR, NAND} control produces violations on the same carrier shape, so a zero there would mean the hypothesis was doing nothing.

attrs.review_focus: Sufficiency is proved and NECESSITY at arity > 2 is untouched (FED-Q3-NEC). The exhaustive spaces are small: they cannot express a witness needing more than two constraints per site, which is exactly how FED-Q3-HYP-S4 hid.

attrs.evidence: Adding NAE₃ destroys the retraction 2 ↦ 0 — it sends the NAE tuple (2,2,0) to (0,0,0) — so End(A) collapses from 6 maps to 2, the core becomes all of D, and Aut has two orbits: {0,2} and {1}, because 1 is the only degree-2 element of R. The property FAILS, and the canonical-query refutation runs: 56 constraints, two sites, both satisfiable, κ_splitBerge = 0, union unsatisfiable. THIS MATTERS BECAUSE IT WAS A LABEL, NOT A CHECK. The round-3 research pass ran an exhaustive space of 287,496 federations over this language under the heading "transitive core, NOT value-symmetric" and reported zero violations of the theorem. The antecedent was never satisfied, so that space corroborated nothing about the theorem — and the counterexample was missed for the most ordinary reason: 56 constraints do not fit in a pool of ≤2 constraints per site over four variables. EXHAUSTION OVER A SPACE TOO SMALL TO HOLD THE WITNESS IS EXACTLY AS BLIND AS A SAMPLE, and it reads as stronger. Every space in §5 now decides its hypothesis before entering.

It does not say a smaller witness cannot exist below that, and for corroboration that is the direction that would matter.
attrs.statement: The language {≠∘f, NAE₃} over |D| = 3 has a transitive core.

attrs.evidence: EQ₃(a,b,q) at site 0 and NAE₃(a,b,q) at site 1. In the instance model the two constraint-nodes form a split Berge 2-cycle, κ_splitBerge = 1, and the theorem is correctly silent — fidelity does fail. Merging the identical scopes gives ONE hyperedge, no Berge cycle at all, κ_splitBerge = 0, and the theorem would then assert fidelity for a federation with no model. A repeated variable INSIDE one scope is harmless: one constraint cannot split a cycle with itself.

attrs.statement: The Berge sufficiency theorem requires constraints to be hyperedge INSTANCES: two constraints on the same scope from two sites are two constraint-nodes. A model that merges identical scopes into one hyperedge makes the theorem false.

attrs.evidence: Not proved. The two-hyperedge construction shows that sharing ≥2 variables is fatal, but a full characterization was not established.
attrs.statement: 'No split Berge cycle' is also NECESSARY for all-Γ sufficiency at arity > 2 (the analogue of FED-Q1-STARSTAR).

attrs.evidence: Membership witnesses are ONE-SIDED and the round-3 research pass claimed more for them than they carry. One satisfying assignment per admitted value proves M ⊆ true projection; nothing proves true projection ⊆ M. A site that under-reports its projection passes every membership check — demonstrated executably — and an omitted feasible value can manufacture a false empty message and hence a false UNSAT. Three distinct objects need distinguishing: a positive SAT certificate (constructive witnesses composing to a global assignment), an exact decision message (needs the exact projection), and a negative/UNSAT certificate (needs proof that excluded values are impossible, or an independently checkable local proof system). Directly relevant to TRVM/WRL-style continuous proof.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6 round-3 audit posed it; the round-4 audit found the direct neighbourhood. ATSERIAS, KOLAITIS & VARDI, "Constraint Propagation as a Proof System", CP 2004 (DOI 10.1007/978-3-540-30201-8_9) gives a sound-and-complete CSP refutation system over axioms, relational joins, projections and weakening, terminating in the empty relation — which is unusually close to what this claim asks for. Two routes follow. (a) TWO-SIDED BY CASES: for each v ∈ M a satisfying subtree assignment with x = v; for each v ∉ M a checkable refutation of subtree ∧ (x = v). Together those give M ⊆ truth AND truth ⊆ M. (b) NATIVE: a join/project derivation whose final derived unary relation IS M, so the verifier checks the relational proof rather than trusting a solver — this mirrors the separator algorithm itself instead of hiding it behind SAT, which is why it is the interesting one for TRVM/WRL. Alternatives to compare: SAT encoding with LRAT/DRAT refutations; pseudo-Boolean with VeriPB-style checking; OBDD representations, which Atserias–Kolaitis–Vardi also discuss.
attrs.review_focus: This is the gap between "the protocol is exact" and "the protocol is trustless", and cell 36b cannot be called proof-carrying until it closes. The comparison to make is certificate size, checker complexity, incremental reuse and compositionality.
attrs.statement: What proof object establishes BOTH inclusion and exclusion for a separator projection, so that a receiving site need not trust the sending site's solver?

attrs.evidence: A bridge block with TWO separators. Site 0 pins v1 = 0 through an OR/NAND triangle, site 1 pins v2 = 0 through another, site 2 holds v1 ≠ v2. Every pairwise intersection at v1 and at v2 is non-empty, every site is satisfiable, κₛ = 0 — and the union has no model, because the bridge block needs the JOINT restriction at both ends. The two-pass protocol catches it. Pairwise agreement is necessary and not sufficient.
attrs.prior_art: Fable 5, round-3 research pass.
attrs.statement: Pairwise non-empty intersection of the sites' projections at each shared separator variable is sufficient for union satisfiability.

assumptions: no split Berge cycle — the carrier hypothesis is still required; only the LANGUAGE hypothesis is dropped
attrs.evidence: This is Yannakakis' 1981 semijoin full reducer / Bernstein–Chiu 1981, and Dechter–Pearl 1989 tree clustering, specialised to singleton separators. Implemented and checked against brute-force satisfiability on every no-split federation of the round-1 space for four languages — OR/NAND, pins-plus-≠, <-and-=, and eq/neq as a control — with zero disagreements, including 6,960 federations that are locally satisfiable and globally unsatisfiable and therefore lie outside any language-wide theorem. This is the operationally important route for cell 36: where a value sort cannot have a transitive core, this still decides.

attrs.prior_art: Yannakakis, Algorithms for Acyclic Database Schemes, VLDB 1981 · Dechter & Pearl, Tree Clustering for Constraint Networks, AI 38 (1989). KNOWN, not re-derived; what is claimed here is that it runs and agrees.
attrs.statement: Under no split Berge cycle, one leaf-to-root pass of exact unary separator projections over the super-block tree decides union satisfiability, with NO hypothesis on the constraint language.

attrs.evidence: NOT CLAIMED AND NOT TRUE IN GENERAL. The protocol removes the GLOBAL cyclic interaction — the federation carrier becomes a tree — but each super-block still has a local CSP to project, which for unrestricted Γ is NP-hard. A tree of hard problems is not an easy problem, and "efficient" must not be published on the strength of the carrier shape. Message size is likewise bounded by |D| bits only for a finite explicit sort; for a large or infinite value sort the message must be symbolic and the bit bound does not transfer. Nor is the message "the smallest" boundary summary: exactness is proved, an information-theoretic lower bound is not. SHARPENED BY THE ROUND-4 AUDIT, in the direction that makes the statement useful rather than only cautionary: for a fixed finite core template Γ, adding singleton relations/constants is polynomial-time equivalent to CSP(Γ) — a standard finite-CSP result — so the exact unary separator projection costs at most |D| satisfiability tests, one per candidate value. Hence FOR FIXED FINITE D AND A TRACTABLE CORE LANGUAGE, separator projection is tractable exactly when the local block CSP is. THE LOCAL CSP IS THE CONTROLLING TERM, not the carrier shape, and that is the correction: the question is not "does a tree carrier make this efficient". Three cautions survive. Unrestricted Γ can make the block CSP NP-hard. For a large or infinite domain, enumerating all separator values is the wrong representation and symbolic query/projection complexity is the real problem. Multi-sorted domains are handled per separator sort, AFTER computing the global core.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6 round-4 audit. The singleton-relation equivalence is standard finite-CSP (Bulatov–Jeavons–Krokhin; the "conservative"/idempotent reduction).
attrs.statement: Is the separator protocol tractable for realistic block languages?

attrs.evidence: Three sites holding x≠y, y≠z, z≠x over |D|=2 — an odd cycle of disequalities, i.e. a 2-colouring of K₃.

attrs.statement: For every federation, if every site is locally satisfiable and every pairwise overlap is consistent, then the union has a model.

attrs.evidence: Each canonical conjunctive query emits one atom per tuple of each relation, so it has Σ|R^A| constraints over |D| variables; two of them glued at the free variable give 2Σ|R^A| constraints over 2|D|−1 variables. Verified as an EQUALITY on the constraint count for six languages, including the case that motivated the question: {≠∘f, NAE₃} over |D|=3 has |≠∘f| = 4 and |NAE₃| = 27−3 = 24, so 2(4+24) = 56 — exactly the refutation whose size defeated the round-3 exhaustive space. The live questions are tightness, worst-case minimum as a function of |D| and the signature, lower-bound families, and whether a smaller orbit-separating pp-formula can be extracted than the full canonical query. attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6’s ruling on R7.4 §8.1, made executable. R7.4 ASSERTED that with no discharged narrowing the typed closure equals the untyped closure and never computed the untyped closure to compare against. It does now, at every seed node. THIS IS THE ZERO-KNOWLEDGE THEOREM AND IT IS THE CORRECT RESULT RATHER THAN A SHORTFALL: sound abstract interpretation deliberately over-approximates, and with no trustworthy narrowing information the safe answer at every reached node is `I know this support edge may propagate impact, but I cannot prove how` — which is ⊤. Proven transfer semantics may then only IMPROVE precision and may never make the result less conservative. R7.4 asked whether typed = untyped means the typed machinery is premature; the ruling taken here is that it is the correct semantic result AND separately evidence that the machinery has no production precision benefit yet, and that those are not in tension.

attrs.evidence: REFUTED AT R7.4 BY GPT-5.6, AND THE CLAIM WAS THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN. The statement asserts a closure `with an undeclared-edge default of ⊤`. The shipped implementation was `for (const k of imp) { if (!narrows || !(k in narrows)) { out.add(k); continue; } ... }` — that is T?(S) = S, IDENTITY, with the comment `undeclared ⇒ identity ⇒ conservative` written beside it as its own justification. The registry sentence and the executable disagreed and the ledger recorded the sentence. Reproduced before the fix: `{correctness}` → `{correctness}`, `{authority}` → `{authority}`, `⊤` → `⊤`. IDENTITY IS A FALSE-NEGATIVE MACHINE — an unknown edge F→G with an upstream `{correctness}` defect that can also invalidate an authority decision reports only `{correctness}`, and the authority impact never enters the worklist, so `ignorance costs precision, never safety` was false as shipped. R7.3'S POSITIVE CONTROL SEEDED ⊤ AND ONLY ⊤, AND identity(⊤) = ⊤: the control agreed with the defect at the single point where the two functions coincide. The `strictly more precise than the untyped closure` conjunct was also true only BECAUSE of the defect — under the correct semantics, with no discharged narrowing, the typed closure EQUALS the untyped one.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's §8.2 ruling on R7.3's own question, and it answers that question against R7.3. R7.3 asked whether ⊤-by-default buys anything or merely relocates trust into a counted pile of narrowings; the ruling is that ⊤ is genuinely valuable AND counting is not enough, because an authored sentence like `correctness cannot cross E5 because …` must not itself change the operational worklist or a well-written paragraph removes an affected descendant from it. The ladder is: no knowledge → ⊤ · declared narrowing → still ⊤ · narrowing plus discharged evidence → apply the narrower T_e. Executed both ways in scripts/emb-impact-closure.mjs §3: E4 declares `confidentiality → ∅` with a full justification and the closure computes ⊤ for it, while the same shape marked `proved` on E5 computes ∅. THE SECOND HALF IS NOT DECORATION — without a discharged control the `apply the narrowing` branch is unreachable by accident, which is exactly the R5.2 defect where the `sampling` qualifier had been named by the consumption rule since randomized_search existed and no record ever reached it. The count of narrowings survives as a PRECISION-DEBT metric and is no longer any part of the safety argument. CORRECTED AT R7.5 — THE PROPOSITION HELD AND THE CONTROL SET DID NOT ESTABLISH IT. operational() is a CONJUNCTION of two guards, `state === proved` and `evidence_ref || synthetic_control`, and E4 — the only declared edge in the R7.4 fixture — FAILED BOTH AT ONCE. Running GPT-5.6’s own registered fault model against the R7.4 tree, M3 (`declared-but-unproved becomes operational`) SURVIVED, and so did its mirror: either guard could be deleted from the source with every check still green. This is the R7.4 lesson at a CONJUNCTION — a control landing where both conjuncts fail together tests neither. E7 (evidence present, discharge not asserted) and E8 (discharge asserted, nothing behind it) now fail one guard each, and both mutants die.

attrs.evidence: The round-3 research pass proposed parameterizing the whole ledger over an ordered commutative monoid {zero, add, leq, convert}. THAT IS NOT ENOUGH FOR THIS LEDGER and is deliberately not implemented. `transfer` needs comparison, SUBTRACTION from a source account, and addition to a destination; a generic commutative monoid has no subtraction. A privacy-loss distribution composes under a monoid operation without having any meaningful "refund this PLD to the treasury". Two abstractions, not one: (A) an allocatable conserved resource, needing at least an ordered cancellative structure with a valid partial subtraction or residuation; (B) an irreversible information accountant, needing only zero / compose / admit-against-a-cap / conservative-guarantee, with no refund. Bridge them only where a real allocation notion exists. This may be cleaner than the current representation of privacy loss as double-entry value transferred to a sink.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, rounds 3 and 4. The round-4 audit named the established neighbourhoods, which is what makes this searchable rather than a blank design question. FOR (A) THE CONSERVED ALLOCATABLE RESOURCE: separation algebras and cancellative partial commutative monoids; preordered partial commutative resource monoids; residuated and partially subtractive ordered monoids. A cancellative additive structure is the attractive one, because under its algebraic order a ≤ b supports a unique residual c with a + c = b where it exists — exactly the shape `transfer` needs. FOR (B) THE MONOTONE ACCOUNTANT: an ordered commutative monoid plus an admissible down-set/filter models composition without any refund; RDP at a fixed order is the canonical additive instance. DO NOT PICK A NAME BY ANALOGY — check that the exact total/partial operations and ordering laws match the kernel before adopting one.

attrs.evidence: PROOF. `admissibleTransfer(L,res,from,to,amt)` is the sole guard on `transfer`, which is the sole balance-mutating primitive among transfer/spend/refill/allocate/charge/use/repair. It requires `amt >= 0`, and for `kind[res] === 'irreversible'` it returns false when `from === SINK`. An accepted transfer therefore changes only `bal[from][res] -= amt` and `bal[to][res] += amt` with `amt >= 0` and `from !== SINK`; so `bal[SINK][res]` is touched only in the `to === SINK` case, where it increases by `amt >= 0`. Non-decreasing follows, and a transfer with `from === SINK` returns INFEASIBLE by the same clause. This is the proposition LED-C9 was reaching for and did not state: LED-C9 quantified over EVERY operation of the module, and `consolidate`/`forget` are operations of the module that are not transfer-mediated.

attrs.evidence: Reproduced. Privacy currencies are real-valued (ρ = Δ²/2σ²), so a real-valued instantiation needs rational or fixed-point amounts, or a tolerance in CB2. NOT FIXED in this round: it is a representation change to a shipped kernel and it was not required by any gate this round set. ROUND 3 narrowed the representation question and rejected one proposed answer. SOUND: exact rationals when the currency is rational; fixed-point with cost rounded UP and cap rounded DOWN is conservative for additive comparisons and never undercounts, while float64 admits unsoundly at a sub-resolution cap. NOT SOUND AS A UNIVERSAL ANSWER: "exact rationals" does not cover nonlinear conversions — log, sqrt, a minimum over RDP orders, PLD discretization — each of which needs its own directed/interval soundness argument. AND CB2 MUST KEEP ITS BRIDGE MEANING: replacing it with "add is associative and commutative" would demote an operational law (charging a pipeline sequentially has the same resource effect as charging the composed cost) into an algebra law about the representation. Keep both, do not substitute one for the other.

attrs.evidence: A terminology error worth correcting before it is encoded. By Rogers–Roth–Ullman–Vadhan 2016 a privacy FILTER is exactly a stopping rule that prevents exceeding a PRE-SPECIFIED budget; an ODOMETER tracks accumulated loss with no pre-specified budget. A fixed target with a stop is therefore a filter problem, and the filter theorems apply to it. THE REAL GAP IS DIFFERENT and is recorded separately: Feldman–Zrnic 2021 gives a clean adaptive filter at a FIXED RDP order α, and choosing the best α after seeing an adaptive transcript is a data-dependent choice the fixed-α theorem does not justify. That needs a simultaneous/multi-order filter theorem or a precommitment with a union argument — LED-RDP-ORDER.

attrs.evidence: SRC-BATES-2015-LPM. Linux Provenance Modules states G1 Complete as `the provenance record be gapless in its description of system activity`, scopes it to CONTROLLED DATA TYPES, and discharges it by placing a provenance hook directly beneath each LSM authorization hook and INHERITING LSM's separately verified complete mediation over that type universe. It declares the gap the placement creates — failed access attempts are not recorded — and relocates tamperproofness to secure boot and TPM attestation rather than closing it. SRC-SALTZER-1975-MEDIATION supplies the contrast: `every access to every object must be checked for authority` fixes no universe, and the universe is therefore a hypothesis of the principle rather than a consequence of it. attrs.statement: AN AUTHORITY CANNOT VALIDATE A SEMANTIC CLAIM USING A PROGRAM RESOLVER SUPPLIED BY THE CLAIMANT. Acceptance takes no proof from its caller — INCLUDING the mapping from semantic identity to semantic program. Re-derivation is only evidence if the authority chose what it re-derived against. The supplier ladder this closes has four rungs and one shape: @1 the caller supplied the implementation LABEL (deriveLocally's third parameter), @2 the registration NAME (registerExecutor), @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence (a launcher's spawn), @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE at acceptance (accept's registry parameter). Any field a caller controls on the path to a verdict becomes the verdict. AN instanceof CHECK DOES NOT CLOSE IT, and a law that read as 'check the type' would invite exactly the wrong repair: a Proxy satisfies the type, and so does a genuine ProgramRegistry the caller populated with a different program. The repair is OWNERSHIP. The registry is BUILT at the authority's construction from canonical program DATA — ProgramRegistry.bind severs it through canonicalBytes — so the authority owns its semantic oracle rather than sharing an object with whoever built it, and no registry parameter crosses execute() or accept() again. bindProgram remains an explicit authority operation and needs no second rule, because ids are content-bound: teaching the authority const(999) gives it a new id and cannot repoint const(5)'s. So every oracle the authority consults is constructor-time — the World reader (round 17), the semantic registry (here), and the execution host with its immutable catalog (derivation.implementation-provenance@4) — and what a caller supplies is an INTENT and a RESULT TO VALIDATE.

attrs.statement: ONE SOURCE PROGRAM UNDER ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS DETERMINES ONE CANONICAL TARGET TERM. lowering_sem_id identifies the lowering SEMANTICS — H over the source core_sem_id, the target term encoding id, the canonical lowering specification and the conformance-vector identity — and is a different object from a record of what happened when a particular program was lowered, which is a LoweringReceipt {program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}. One id must not silently answer both 'which lowering semantics is this?' and 'what did lowering do here?'. THE INSTRUMENT IS RE-LOWERING, NOT A FILM. A semantic film is evidence for a TRANSITION SYSTEM; lowering is a relation DeriveProgram -> TargetTerm. Filming it would invent a sequence of internal compiler steps and make implementation strategy semantic — the mistake the read-order ruling refused when it kept access order out of the footprint. Verification is: re-lower the program independently under lowering_sem_id, canonicalise, and require target_term_sem_id to agree. DEFERRED AND NAMED: whether lowering is PARAMETERIZED (program -> target term with input ports, inputs arriving at execution, so target_term_sem_id is a function of the program alone) or INSTANTIATED (program + canonical_inputs -> closed target term, in which case the identity must say so). The first witness uses inputs={} and does not decide it. That decision comes BEFORE the input op, because an unstated variable inside target_term_sem_id is the hidden-identity bug class round 16 exists to prevent.

B1.2.1 adds emit-is-not-a-hidden-relation (three emitter mutations move the instantiation id and not lowering's; two per-op rule mutations move lowering's and not instantiation's; a template-grammar mutation moves both and the template-encoding id; every name in refusal_semantics is driven to a refusal) and chain-identities-stay-distinct, whose set is DERIVED from REFINEMENT_CHAIN rather than hand-typed.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B2, when the relation it describes became EXECUTABLE, and kept as history. Revision 2 described a decided-and-unbuilt architecture; nothing in it was false and no verdict rested on behaviour that did not exist -- instantiate() had never run. What changed is that the claims are now witnessed rather than declared.
attrs.statement: ONE SOURCE PROGRAM UNDER ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS DETERMINES ONE CANONICAL TARGET TERM. lowering_sem_id identifies the lowering SEMANTICS — H over the LOWERING SEMANTICS alone: the source core_sem_id, the id of its CODOMAIN encoding (TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1, and NOT the executable encoding, which is instantiation's codomain), the per-op lowering map, the refusal vocabulary lower() can actually produce, and totality on the fragment — and is a different object from a record of what happened when a particular program was lowered, which is a LoweringReceipt {program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_template_sem_id}. One id must not silently answer both 'which lowering semantics is this?' and 'what did lowering do here?'. THE INSTRUMENT IS RE-LOWERING, NOT A FILM. A semantic film is evidence for a TRANSITION SYSTEM; lowering is a relation DeriveProgram -> TargetTerm. Filming it would invent a sequence of internal compiler steps and make implementation strategy semantic — the mistake the read-order ruling refused when it kept access order out of the footprint. Verification is: re-lower the program independently under lowering_sem_id, canonicalise, and require target_term_sem_id to agree. DECIDED AT B1 AND BUILT AT B1.2, and the earlier framing was wrong: whether lowering is PARAMETERIZED (program -> target term with input ports, so target_term_sem_id is a function of the program alone) or INSTANTIATED (program + canonical_inputs -> closed target term) was a FALSE CHOICE. The template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed, so there are TWO relations with two identities and lowering's codomain is the TEMPLATE. This statement said DEFERRED for three passes after the decision, and printed the pre-B1.2 receipt shape for one -- while grid_check REQUIRED the deferred wording, which turns a check into a ratchet holding a stale record in place. See derivation.instantiation-identity@3. CORRECTED AT B1.2.1, AND emit() WAS A HIDDEN SEMANTIC RELATION. B1.2 moved lowering's codomain onto the template and left BOTH encoding commitments pointing where they had pointed when there was no template. MEASURED: change the add combinator and nothing else, and the executable term's bytes change while INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, target_template_sem_id and the template-encoding id all stand still -- so the identity of the relation that PRODUCES those bytes did not move. LOWERING_SEM_ID moved instead, which is the same mistake facing the other way. UNDER-BOUND: INSTANTIATION_SEMANTICS named its codomain in PROSE, 'TRVM-TERM-CANON-v1 / ic32 executable text, via emit()', so the whole executable encoding reached the relation's identity only as a symbol name inside an English sentence -- a label anyone may claim, the objection the primitive ruling already raised against a bare componentReachability. OVER-BOUND: LOWERING_SEMANTICS still carried the entire TARGET_ENCODING, a pre-template leftover of the same class as the LoweringReceipt that kept ending at target_term_sem_id, which B1.2 fixed one declaration away and missed here; an emitter change therefore re-identified every LoweringReceipt ever issued, for a relation lowering does not perform. THE RULE: A RELATION'S IDENTITY MUST COMMIT, BY CONTENT AND NOT BY NAME, TO EXACTLY THE ENCODINGS OF ITS OWN DOMAIN AND CODOMAIN -- no more and no fewer. Lowering commits to TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1 and to its own per-op map; instantiation commits to the template encoding as domain and to TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID as codomain, and EMISSION IS INSIDE THE INSTANTIATION RELATION. That last is a ruling with a stated trigger for revisiting it rather than a convenience: a third relation with its own emission_sem_id is the more faithful decomposition, because a correct port substitution can coexist with an incorrect emitter, and it is NOT taken while emit() is neither independently reused nor independently theorem-bearing. MEASURED IN THREE DIRECTIONS: an emitter change moves the instantiation id ALONE, a per-op lowering-rule change moves lowering's ALONE, and a template-grammar change moves BOTH because it is the boundary they share. REMOVING THE LEFTOVER BINDING EXPOSED A SECOND GAP: nothing in the hashed lowering semantics said that a const becomes a church node or that add's operand order is preserved -- B1.1 froze the `input` rule and const and add were left implicit -- so const(n) lowering to church(n+1) would have contradicted no sentence. An identity that cannot move when its map changes is the same defect as one that moves when its map has not. AND THE REFUSAL VOCABULARIES WERE CROSSED: the executable encoding listed four lower-* source-fragment refusals that cannot arise while emitting, while lowering claimed emit-unbound-port and template-malformed, neither reachable from lower(), which emits only zero-port templates it built itself. Each list now belongs to the record that owns it, and every name lowering claims is driven to a refusal by the witness.

attrs.statement: TRVM-DERIVE-CORE-v1 is FROZEN and its identity is content-bound. Changing what add means moves core_sem_id and therefore every program_sem_id, which is the property that makes the identity semantic rather than syntactic. A prim extension bumps the core version and every program id with it: a program written against a different language is a different program.

attrs.statement: THE CANONICAL EMITTER DETERMINISTICALLY REALISES ITS DECLARED RELATION, over a FAMILY of fixtures rather than the one witness it had. closed_template_sem_id -(emission_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, and a conformance record is those three fields and no more: the relation's id is CONSTANT across every fixture, because a per-fixture emission id would identify invocations rather than the relation -- instantiation-identity@1's finding, one relation downstream. VERIFICATION IS BY RECONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY SELF-AGREEMENT: the verifier rebuilds the closed template from (program, inputs), re-emits through the canonical emitter, and canonicalises with an oracle IT WAS HANDED rather than one the emitter chose. An emitter that produced the artifact and certified its identity would verify a wrong emission against itself. EMISSION IS A FUNCTION OF THE CLOSED TEMPLATE AND NOT OF THE PROGRAM, which the family MEASURES rather than assumes: add(const 2, const 3) and add(input x, input y) closed with {x:2,y:3} are THE SAME CLOSED TEMPLATE and emit identically. Instantiation has already erased the difference between a literal and a port bound to that literal, and an emitter producing different bytes for those two would be reading something it is not entitled to see. The check is the implication in the direction that can be wrong -- equal domain implies equal codomain, different domain implies no collision -- rather than a blanket injectivity claim that would be false. TWO PROPERTIES THAT LOOK CONTRADICTORY ARE PROVED SEPARATELY. CANONICAL DETERMINISM: a structural change to the emitter moves target_term_sem_id and the receipt carrying it is REFUSED. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE: that same alternate emitter's output decodes to the same outcome. The first says the relation is a function; the second says target_term_sem_id identifies THIS emitter's output rather than the term's meaning. Collapsing them yields either 'reordering is a semantic change' or 'emission may drift as long as the answer matches', and the second is how a compiler stops being reproducible quietly. AND THE MUTATION THAT EXHIBITS THE PAIR HAD TO BE MEASURED. An ALPHA-EQUIVALENT alternate emitter produces the IDENTICAL target_term_sem_id on every fixture -- the canonical signature is byte-equivariant under alpha-renaming and label permutation by asserted law (L-BYTES-1) -- so renaming cannot witness this at all and the adversary must be STRUCTURAL. Reordering add's operands is meaning-preserving on THIS fragment because addition commutes, and would not be for a non-commutative operator; the caveat is part of the law rather than a footnote to it. NO NATIVE FILM IS REQUIRED OR USED. The transition relation carries its own evidence, and defining the emitter's correctness by what its output computes would put the runtime inside the compiler's contract -- the layer collapse lowering_spike.layer_separation exists to refuse. A downstream composition runs last and is LABELLED an integration theorem; every conformance case stands without it.
