AND AT B7 THE FRAGMENT WIDENS, WHICH IS THE FIRST TIME THIS RELATION HAS HAD TO SAY WHAT IT CANNOT DO. `sub` is the first construct whose SOURCE meaning does not fit in the TARGET: the frozen core's `sub` is true subtraction and evaluates sub(2,3) to -1, while the executable encoding represents NON-NEGATIVE Church naturals and has no image for -1. THE SOURCE LANGUAGE THEREFORE PROPERLY CONTAINS THE REPRESENTABLE TARGET FRAGMENT, which is what a partial compiler is, and emission refuses by name -- emit-sub-underflow -- against its own CODOMAIN. THREE OTHER PLACES TO PUT THAT REFUSAL WERE CONSIDERED AND ARE WRONG. SATURATION is a miscompilation and not a design choice: raw Church subtraction ((n PRED) m) normalises to 0 whenever n >= m, so compiling the core's sub onto it answers 0 where the source says -1 -- and the damage is not confined to the root, because (2-3)+2 then decodes to 2 against the source's 1, an answer that is itself perfectly representable and therefore invisible to any check on the RESULT. A LOWERING PRECONDITION cannot be written at all: sub(input x, input y) has no underflow fact until an invocation binds the ports, so one template emits under {x:5,y:2} and refuses under {x:2,y:5}, and at lowering they are the same object. A SOURCE REFUSAL would change the language to suit the compiler and move CORE_SEM_ID, re-identifying every program ever written. AND THIS IS NOT SOURCE-REFUSAL TO TARGET-REFUSAL PRESERVATION AND MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS PROGRESS ON IT: for sub(2,3) the source DOES NOT REFUSE, it evaluates to -1 correctly, and the compiler declines. No target term is produced, so no target outcome exists and none is claimed; the evidence says so rather than leaving the absence to be read as a gap. THE DECISION IS TAKEN BEFORE ANY KNOB IS READ. Whether a closed template has an image is a property of the template and the codomain, not a serialization choice, so representability is checked before the profile is validated and no profile -- including two deliberately broken ones -- can turn a domain refusal into an acceptance or into a different refusal. AND EMISSION EMITS SUBTRACTION RATHER THAN COMPUTING IT. The representability walk evaluates the closed template under the source arithmetic and computes exactly the value a constant folder would return, then DISCARDS it: every emitting sub fixture carries real PRED structure, is longer than emit(church(itsOwnValue)) would be, and is reduced by the runtime under its own interaction-net dynamics -- 96 frames over APP-LAM, APP-SUP, DUP-LAM and DUP-SUP= for sub(5,2), where a folded numeral would reduce in zero. Folding would make the integration theorem a theorem about the compiler's own walk. AND THE OPERAND SWAP HAS CHANGED SIDES EXACTLY AS @5 PREDICTED. E-8b was meaning-preserving only because addition commutes; for sub it is a FALSIFIER for the opposite property, that operand order IS semantic -- E-10 sub(5,2) emits and E-17 sub(2,5) is refused over the same two operands with the fields exchanged. Its applicable set EXCLUDES BY NAME any fixture whose two operands are byte-equal, because sub(2,2) is its own swap and a symmetric pair cannot reveal order-sensitivity -- INSTANTIATION_FALSIFIERS I-4c's own species, and the first draft of the case included them and failed.

attrs.evidence: probe_reread_v13_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against frozen v0.12.0 copies of execute() and accept() — the authority issues psem-82eee05e… (const 5), executes psem-3b198d80… (const 999), the native worker returns 999, and acceptance of that result under a fresh time-varying request returns {ok:true, validated:true, implementation_provenance:'observed'} while the frozen issued request refuses it as result-program-mismatch. 5/5 confined live: a time-varying request is read EXACTLY ONCE by execute() and the program that runs is the one authorized; acceptance reads a time-varying request once and a time-varying result once; wasIssued() returns the deep-frozen issued request and a stranger authority still gets grant-not-issued-by-this-authority and no request; a function-carrying result, a ProgramRegistry in the request slot and a closure-carrying intent each die at the entry rather than halfway through; and the ladder is one frozen record of seven rungs. derive_realm_battery.mjs case 'every-entrypoint-reads-its-argument-once' enumerates nine entrypoints and measures reads against a one-read-per-field floor: 7/7, 1/1, 11/11, 11/11, 11/11, 18/18, 11/11, 18/18, 2/2. Reintroducing the defect in execute() alone moves that to 33/11 and the case names the offending entrypoint. P-7c: 3/3 frozen breaches and 6/6 live confinements in the same probe — the frozen v0.2.1 read ordering splits the keyed request from the executed one, and the live host reads its invocation exactly once, answers 5 for the request it keyed, and holds the observation under the bytes that ran and not under the ones that did not. derive_realm_battery.mjs case 'meta-operations-stop-at-one-traversal' hands twelve entrypoints — including the reusable exports — a RECURSIVELY Proxy-wrapped argument counting ownKeys, getOwnPropertyDescriptor, getPrototypeOf, has and get, and requires each to equal a single ownCanonical traversal exactly (e.g. wasIssued/req gOPD:11 get:11 getPrototypeOf:6 ownKeys:6).
attrs.statement: EVERY AUTHORITY OPERATION CONSUMES EITHER AN AUTHORITY-OWNED OBJECT OR ONE CANONICAL SNAPSHOT MADE AT ENTRY. NO TRUST DECISION AUTHENTICATES ONE READ OF EXTERNAL STATE AND EXERCISES AUTHORITY USING ANOTHER. derivation.owned-snapshot@1 stated this rule for structures BECOMING authority state and was correct; this is the same rule reaching method ARGUMENTS, where it had never been applied. wasIssued(req) hashed one read of every field and proved 'these bytes are the request I issued'; execute() then read the caller's object again for the implementation family, again when the host canonicalised the invocation, and again when the worker structured-cloned it. A request whose program_sem_id answers const(5) to the first read and const(999) to every read after it is therefore ISSUED as one program and EXECUTED as another. Both programs are genuinely in the authority's own registry, so nothing is malformed, no identity is forged and nothing fails closed: acceptance re-derives 999 against 999, finds the provenance of an execution the authority really drove, and returns implementation_provenance 'observed' for a result the authority never authorized. THE SAME RESULT PAIRED WITH THE FROZEN ISSUED REQUEST IS REFUSED as result-program-mismatch, which is what makes this a forgery rather than fail-closed hygiene — the entire difference is the caller's retained ownership. THE REPAIR IS NOT A FRESHER HASH. Hashing again would authenticate a second read and leave a third. The issuance table keeps the REQUEST and not merely its identity, because a table of hashes can answer 'were these bytes issued?' and cannot answer 'what did I issue?', and every method that needed the second question had no choice but to re-read the caller; wasIssued() returns that owned request and execute() and accept() read it. THE RESULT SIDE WAS CLOSED IN THE SAME ROUND, ONE ARGUMENT TO THE RIGHT, without waiting for its own witness: `res` was consulted by six checks in sequence, and a caller who cannot vary the request while it is validated can still vary the result. Seven rungs, one shape — LABEL, NAME, ACTION, SEMANTIC ORACLE, AUTHORITY-BEARING OBJECT, MUTABLE DATA READ TWICE, MUTABLE DATA AUTHENTICATED ONCE — and @6 and @7 are one rule at two moments: validate X then store X', authenticate X then act with X'. The mechanism is one exported ownCanonical() called at the top of every method taking a non-root data argument, and the enforcement is a battery case that enumerates the authority's entrypoints and fails when any argument is read more than once per field, because a law applied only where a witness has been written is a law with the reach of its witnesses. AND THE OBLIGATION BELONGS TO THE ENTRYPOINT, NOT TO ITS POLITEST CALLER. ObservedExecutionHost.run() keyed the observation over canonicalBytes(invocation) and then handed the same live object to the transport, so an invocation honest on read 1 and hostile on read 2 was KEYED under one request and EXECUTED as another, leaving a true-looking observation for an execution that did not happen — in the table round 23 built precisely so that relabelling would move the key. That path is unreachable through DerivationAuthority.execute, whose invocation is assembled from owned parts; the host is nonetheless exported, FilmAuthority and lowering_check drive it directly, and it writes the observation table, so it is an authority operation carrying the rule itself (P-7c). THE REUSABLE VALIDATORS CARRY THE SAME OBLIGATION AT THEIR OWN EDGE. checkRequest, checkIntent, checkResult, deriveLocally and validateForeignResult reread their arguments field by field — one checkRequest call over a Proxy-wrapped request touched ownKeys 2, getOwnPropertyDescriptor 10, getPrototypeOf 1, get 13 and has 1 — so 'a pure function over data the caller already owns' is the second half of a sentence whose first half was a precondition nothing enforced. The implementations are named ...Owned and the precondition is mechanical inside the authority, which passes only issued/ownRes/ownIntent; the exported names snapshot once and delegate, so a second authority built on them cannot recreate P-7 without writing new trust logic. This is an API-boundary hazard predicted by the law, not a false verdict, and it is deliberately not numbered as a rung. AND HISTORICAL FACT IS NOT A FUNCTION OF CURRENT CONFIGURATION. Acceptance rebuilt the invocation it asked the observation table about out of this.#registry.image(), so bindProgram() — an explicit, legitimate authority operation — grew that image and made the provenance of an earlier genuine execution vanish: execute(A), accept -> observed, bindProgram(B), accept the same request and result -> implementation-provenance-unavailable. It fails closed and forges nothing, and it is still wrong, because unrelated future installation must not erase the evidence of what previously ran. execute() now records the canonical invocation bytes THE HOST KEYED, acceptance looks those up, and the records are a list because the same request run before and after a bind is two genuinely different invocations and both happened; observations across them are MERGED rather than first-hit, for the round-24 reason that reporting one launch as though it were the only one overclaims. DECLARED OPEN: object-form canonicalisation MAY INVOKE JavaScript accessor and Proxy behaviour while capturing its snapshot — reading {get x(){}} executes a function, and a Proxy runs ownKeys/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/getPrototypeOf/has/get traps during serialisation. What is established is that no such behaviour SURVIVES the snapshot or participates in any later authority decision, measured as a full-trap surface equal to exactly one ownCanonical traversal. The stronger property — no hostile same-realm code executes at ingestion at all — is unreachable for any API whose boundary is an arbitrary JavaScript object, and needs a serialized-wire boundary (canonical text -> authority-owned parser -> data), which is not built. Relatedly, the read-count enumeration is a REGRESSION DETECTOR AND NOT A TERMINATING PROOF: Object.keys(x) twice leaves an accessor's read count at zero while touching the object twice, so a field-read counter sees only the `get` category and the meta-operation instrument covers the rest.

attrs.evidence: probe_closureenv_repro.mjs against World 0.11.0 — B is support_changed and re-derives to 1005 where an honest B is 5, in both the coordinator and the World, with derivation_id unchanged and the pass not aborted. Frozen and deliberately NOT gated: the probe exits 0 because it documents a boundary rather than a regression. Four ownership rounds (9D.1 raw maps and caller objects, 9D.2 nested values, 9D.3 fail-open ownership, and this) converged on the conclusion that an arbitrary closure is an unbounded capability container — an architectural boundary, not a missing Object.freeze.
attrs.statement: A derivation's authority must be bounded by what the coordinator can own. Under the current same-realm arbitrary-closure measureFn API it is NOT, and this law is FALSIFIED BY DESIGN rather than repaired: capturing an arbitrary callable does not capture its semantics, and a function reference may retain mutable authority that is neither enumerable nor ownable. The witness needs no mutable object at all — a `let bias = 0` shared by two closures. Object.freeze, deepFreeze, structuredClone, canonicalBytes, #private fields, GuardedStore and the pass-entry snapshot are all INAPPLICABLE, because JavaScript provides no mechanism to enumerate, copy, canonicalize or freeze a captured lexical environment; freezing measureFn itself does not help either. A second theorem fails with it: derivation_id is computed from measure/predicate/inputs and therefore does NOT identify a derivation's semantics — the witness holds derivation_id constant while behaviour changes from fb to fb+1000. Tolerable as an acknowledged limit of the closure API; NOT tolerable once semantic films assert that an identified program performed a particular transition. Closure is by REPLACING the API, not by hardening it: see realm_roadmap.

attrs.evidence: probe_traceforge_v06_repro.mjs — T-1: a program reading a then b, with ONLY the trace reversed and the canonical footprint and value untouched, passed validateForeignResult and was accepted with validated + fresh_at_check under v0.5.0. checkResult compared the footprint to the SET of the trace, which a reversal does not change, and the semantic projection excluded the trace — so the one field carrying execution evidence was the one field nothing looked at. 1/1 reproduces against the frozen v0.5.0 validation and 4/4 confined live. derive_battery.mjs: trace-is-outside-the-semantic-projection, plus the envelope schema checks in checkResult.
attrs.statement: NON-SEMANTIC DOES NOT MEAN UNVERIFIED. A DeriveResult carries two explicit envelopes with different trust rules. semantic_result (value, witness, support, read_footprint) determines portable meaning and is what cross-implementation validation compares. execution_evidence (implementation_id, read_trace) carries conformance and provenance: it is EXCLUDED from that comparison and NOT excluded from checking. The core fixes evaluation order — depth-first, `a` before `b` — precisely so that refusals and traces reproduce, so a returned trace that disagrees with the authority's own re-derivation is a CONFORMANCE failure of the implementation rather than a disagreement about the program, and it is refused as trace-nonconforming. The two verdicts are reported SEPARATELY — semantic_agreement and trace_conforms — because 'same meaning, different strategy' and 'wrong answer' are different diagnoses. The flat shape was part of the defect: a field sitting beside value and read_footprint reads as authenticated by the same machinery as its neighbours. Later the semantic film supersedes the trace check and lives in this same envelope.

attrs.evidence: probe_stalegrant_v03_repro.mjs: grant cut at fb@1=5, derived, World moved to fb@2=9 — checkResult PASS, footprintWithinGrant PASS, validateForeignResult PASS, all three CORRECT, and acceptance refuses 'stale-read: fb granted@1 live@2'. Plus the negative half (unrelated-write-ignored) and the scope half (stale-scope: kind:node, a node joining a query with no exact read moving). derive_battery.mjs: freshness-is-not-containment, unrelated-write-does-not-invalidate, acceptance-does-not-claim-committable. derive_realm_battery.mjs: intent-to-acceptance across a real worker.
attrs.statement: Containment and freshness are different questions and a protocol needs both. footprintWithinGrant asks a HISTORICAL question — was every claimed read inside the snapshot this derivation received? validateFootprintFresh asks a TEMPORAL one — are those dependencies still current at the moment of acceptance? Both can be satisfied about a World that has moved, so re-derivation against the grant can never detect staleness: executor and authority agree perfectly about an old snapshot. Freshness keys on the FOOTPRINT and never on a global vclock — an unrelated write must not invalidate a derivation that did not depend on it, or the grant/footprint separation is undone from the other side. Exact reads compare versions; scope predicates compare digests, which is the World's phantom-scope case reaching the derivation boundary. ACCEPTANCE DOES NOT ESTABLISH COMMITTABILITY. One call cannot: the World can move between it returning and the caller applying. It establishes `validated` and `fresh_at_check` — an observation at a moment — and the composition that commits belongs to the World: acquire the authoritative lock, accept, deterministic prepared apply with no hostile callback in between, seal the receipt, release. No lock capability is exported to reach that, because rounds 9B-9C are the record of what happens when transaction authority gets passed around.

attrs.evidence: derive_battery.mjs: grant-not-reachable-as-input, footprint-is-the-access-subset (a 3-resource grant against a 1-entry footprint), grant-id-binds-the-snapshot (a swapped snapshot under the original grant_id is refused request-grant-id-mismatch), footprint-validated-independently (footprint-ungranted-read / footprint-version-mismatch, both fired on an otherwise honest result), witness-matches-footprint. derive_realm_battery.mjs repeats the input-reachability and forged-footprint cases across a real worker. The v0.1.0 defect is frozen as W-1 in probe_derivegrant_v02_repro.mjs and must keep reproducing there. GRANTING MODEL, decided rather than defaulted: snapshot (A) not read-RPC (B) — deterministic, films cleanly, no cross-realm round trip per primitive. Its cost is least-authority, since the grant may reveal more than the program reads; confidentiality against the derivation realm is the stated trigger to revisit.
attrs.statement: The authority grant and the read footprint are TWO evidence objects and may not be collapsed into one. The grant (read_grants, named by grant_id = H(canonical read_grants)) is a CAPABILITY record: what the authority made available, resolved on the authoritative side, deliberately permitted to be broader than what is read because under data-dependent traversal the needed subset is not knowable in advance. The footprint is the DEPENDENCY record: what the program actually consumed through a tracked read or scope, recorded by the evaluator on access. Freshness, invalidation, replay and support analysis key on the footprint alone — defining it as the grant would over-invalidate every derivation whose grant was wider than its reads, which under snapshot granting is all of them. The authority validates the footprint as a SUBSET of the grant, at the granted versions and scope digests, on its own evidence and BEFORE any re-derivation.

attrs.evidence: probe_issuebind_v05_repro.mjs, 3/3 reproduced against the frozen draft and 4/4 confined live. I-1: swapping canonical_inputs under an untouched request_id and grant_id passed wasIssued, derived 1005 where an honest request derives 5, and was accepted as committable. I-2: authorize(intent, {canonical_inputs:{bias:1000}}) produced an AUTHORITY-ISSUED request evaluating to 1005. I-3: acceptance with the issuer argument OMITTED accepted a wholly self-made request, and a fake liveReader replaying the granted version turned a stale-read refusal back into an acceptance. derive_battery.mjs: issuance-binds-the-whole-request, request-sem-id-recomputes, authorize-options-whitelisted, issued-request-is-owned-and-frozen, intent-schema-closed, authority-requires-a-world.
attrs.statement: An authority-issued request authenticates THE WHOLE REQUEST, and acceptance takes no proof from its caller. grant_id is a hash of the grant and a hash authenticates content to itself, so it proves integrity and says nothing about issuance; binding request_id to grant_id answers 'was this issued?' about a GRANT while the thing being accepted is a REQUEST. Issuance therefore records request_id -> request_sem_id = H(canonical request), recomputed at acceptance, so any change to any field is a different request rather than the same request with different content. The authority is the only constructor of a DeriveRequest; a caller submits a DeriveIntent and may REQUEST exactly one thing, expected_implementation_id, which is a requirement on the executor rather than authority content — an open options bag spread after the authority's own fields is a caller writing authority content. Acceptance is a METHOD on the authority, closing over its issuance table and its live World reader: a free function taking those as parameters, with the issuer defaulting to absent, lets the caller supply both proofs of its own authority. The issued request is owned through canonicalBytes and deep-frozen as defence in depth, not as the boundary — the binding is the boundary. A signature or MAC is added when, and only when, the grant crosses a real trust boundary, is persisted and replayed later, is delegated between authorities, or must be proved to an independent verifier.

attrs.evidence: probe_hostown_v11_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against a frozen v0.10.0 guard — P-5, where a two-method subclass yields ok/validated/fresh_at_check with provenance 'observed', implementation_id impl-c-fake-v1 and executable_artifact_id 'fake-artifact' while run() would throw if it were called; and P-5b, which shows the tighter prototype check would have excluded the subclass and still admitted a Proxy over a genuine host. 4/4 confined live: the host is built from catalog data, both an EvilHost and a GENUINE ObservedExecutionHost are refused in the catalog position because neither is a catalog, editing the caller's catalog object after construction reaches nothing, the authority exposes zero own properties and is frozen with the host behind a #private field, and the five rungs are asserted as a set. derive_realm_battery.mjs 20/20, derive_battery.mjs 45/45, bridge/film_check.mjs 14/14 with FilmAuthority taking catalog data for the same reason.
attrs.statement: AN AUTHORITY-BEARING OBJECT MAY NOT BE SUPPLIED TO THE AUTHORITY THAT WILL TRUST IT. An `instanceof` guard is satisfied by a subclass: two overridden methods — run() that never runs and observationOf() that answers whatever it likes — pass `host instanceof ObservedExecutionHost` while bypassing the catalog, the digest, hash-then-launch and the observation table, all of which remain perfectly correct and perfectly unconsulted. Acceptance then reports implementation_provenance 'observed' for an implementation that never ran. THE QUESTION IS NOT WHAT THE OBJECT IS DESCENDED FROM. THE QUESTION IS WHO BUILT IT. So the repair is not a tighter predicate — Object.getPrototypeOf(host) === ObservedExecutionHost.prototype excludes the subclass and admits a Proxy, and would be derivation.acceptance-authority@1's mistake with a longer expression. The authority takes an EXECUTOR CATALOG, which is data, and constructs the host itself against its module's own class binding, which no caller can substitute. Every authority with such a parameter does the same, because this is a property of the PARAMETER and not of any one class. This is the fifth rung of one ladder: @1 the implementation LABEL, @2 the registration NAME, @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence, @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE at acceptance, @5 the EXECUTION-AUTHORITY OBJECT itself. Each rung sat in the parameter that had stopped being examined because it was 'obviously infrastructure'. What a caller supplies is an INTENT, a RESULT TO VALIDATE, and — at construction only — the DATA every oracle is built from.

attrs.evidence: derive_battery.mjs: implementation-id-asserted, implementation-requirement-refused, implementation-id-well-formed, semantic-projection-is-portable (a result stamped impl-c-derive-v0.2.0 validates and its provenance is reported rather than compared away), implementation-requirement-checked-on-result. derive_realm_battery.mjs: executor-asserts-implementation across the worker boundary, and cross-implementation-shape — which is the SHAPE a real C implementation plugs into and explicitly not a claim that one exists. The v0.1.0 defect is frozen as W-2: a request asserting impl-c-pretend-v9 was executed by the JS evaluator and returned success, with no implementation_id in the result at all.
attrs.revision_note: KEPT AS THE RECORD OF A FALSE CLAIM, shipped for seven rounds. @1 said 'A caller therefore cannot cause a result to claim an implementation that did not produce it' and 'this closes IMPERSONATION and does not yet establish PROVENANCE'. The first half was false. deriveLocally took the implementation identity as a PARAMETER, so a caller could run the JS evaluator and stamp its honest output 'impl-c-derive-…', after which acceptance compared the caller's expectation against the caller's own label — a claim against a claim — and returned ok with trace_conforms:true, which made the forgery read as better attested than an unforged result. Reproduced as P-1 in probe_execclaim_v07_repro.mjs. The declared-open item was also mis-scoped: hashing the executable would NOT have closed it, because a digest carried inside the same untrusted result is still self-asserted.
attrs.statement: Execution identity is ASSERTED BY THE EXECUTOR and may only be REQUIRED by the caller. DeriveResult carries implementation_id, emitted by the evaluator that ran; DeriveRequest carries at most expected_implementation_id, which an executor that cannot satisfy it refuses by name. A caller therefore cannot cause a result to claim an implementation that did not produce it. The field is excluded from the semantic projection that cross-implementation validation compares, which is what lets a C result and a JS result of the same program_sem_id agree while their provenance stays distinguishable — the film_identity_forward_declaration split, made operative. DECLARED OPEN: implementation_id is a declared constant, not a digest of executable bytes, so this closes IMPERSONATION and does not yet establish PROVENANCE — a modified JS worker still emits impl-js-derive-v0.2.0. Binding it to a source/binary digest is the next revision and is named here rather than implied.

attrs.evidence: probe_execclaim_v07_repro.mjs: P-1 reproduces against the frozen v0.6.0 acceptance (JS produces every byte, the caller chooses the label, accept returns ok with implementation_id impl-c-derive-v0.6.0 and trace_conforms true) and 6/6 confined live — the caller cannot select a label at all; provenance is 'observed' only with a host handle and 'unavailable' without one, with NO implementation_id reported in that case; a C claim against an observed JS executor is refused; a C requirement with no observation is refused as unavailable; and an executor handle carries a private Symbol the authority minted so it cannot be fabricated. derive_battery.mjs: provenance-requires-observation, claim-checked-against-observation, executor-handles-are-authority-issued, registered-identity-well-formed, validator-does-not-do-provenance, acceptance-success-shape-narrow. trace_conforms is removed from the acceptance success shape — redundant there, and a boolean per check invites weighing them — while staying in the validator and in the failure diagnostics where semantic_agreement:true + trace_conforms:false is the distinction worth having.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED, and kept as the record of a mechanism that did not do what its own statement said. @2 opened 'AN EXECUTION CLAIM IS NOT PROVENANCE' — which is right and survives into @3 — and then named as its mechanism 'the authority records what it launched via an authority-issued executor handle'. It launched nothing. registerExecutor(implementation_id) took a STRING, put it in a private Map, and returned a handle carrying a private Symbol; the Symbol proved that this authority minted this handle and nothing about any execution. So P-1 did not close, it MOVED: v0.6 let the caller choose the identity at deriveLocally(), v0.7 let it choose the identity at registerExecutor(). And accept(registry, req, res, executor = null) put a proof back in the caller's hands — the exact shape round 17 removed from issuance, one level up — so even a registration that really launched C could have had its handle paired with bytes produced elsewhere. Frozen as P-2 and P-2b in probe_execreg_v08_repro.mjs, which reproduces both against a verbatim frozen copy.
attrs.statement: AN EXECUTION CLAIM IS NOT PROVENANCE. A canonical result arriving from outside is an untrusted execution CLAIM however perfect its bytes are, and no property of the result can establish which executor produced it — not a conforming trace, not a version string, and not a digest of the executable, because a digest carried inside the same untrusted result is self-asserted too. The only thing here that is not a claim is what the HOST OBSERVED IT LAUNCH. So: an implementation's identity comes from the implementation and never from a caller-supplied parameter; validateForeignResult establishes semantic agreement and trace conformance and explicitly NOT provenance, reporting implementation_claimed rather than certifying it; the authority records what it launched via an authority-issued executor handle; and acceptance compares the request's expected_implementation_id against the OBSERVATION, refuses implementation-claim-contradicts-observation when the result's label disagrees with it, and answers implementation-provenance-unavailable — never 'verified' — where no observation exists. Three distinct objects, and round 19's two envelopes were one short: semantic_result is portable MEANING, execution_evidence is the execution CLAIM, and the host's observation is the only OBSERVATION. DECLARED OPEN, now correctly scoped: WHAT identity a native executable should register — a trusted launcher hashing the binary it is about to exec — is unbuilt. WHETHER an independent observation exists at all is no longer optional.

attrs.evidence: probe_execreg_v08_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against a verbatim frozen v0.7.0 — P-2 (registerExecutor('impl-c-derive-…') launches nothing, JS produces every byte, the result is relabelled C, and acceptance returns ok with implementation_provenance 'observed') and P-2b (ONE handle provenances TWO unrelated executions, because a handle binds neither a request nor a set of bytes) — and 5/5 confined against live. derive_realm_battery.mjs 19/19, where cases 11-18 exercise the launch contract end to end: an authority-driven execution reporting all three identities, naming C without launching C, relabelling after observation, a second authority holding no observation for the same bytes, an unnamed artifact refused before spawn, a launcher that declares someone else's files being identified as those files, the naming policy refusing both rebinding directions, and the structural absence of registerExecutor. derive_battery.mjs: in-process-has-no-provenance, requirement-without-observation-refused, no-caller-supplied-provenance, naming-policy-well-formed. grid_check asserts the source-level invariants: accept's exact parameter list, the single writer of the observation table, and that the authority — never the launcher — hashes the artifact.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED, and it was right about the half it named. @3 said the authority must read and hash the artifact ITSELF rather than believe a name, and that stands. What it did not say is that hashing the declaration establishes nothing about what was then invoked. v0.8.0's launcher carried `artifact_files` (the evidence, honestly hashed) beside `spawn` (an independent caller-controlled action), two fields of one object with nothing binding them — so declaring the genuine JS worker closure, naming that digest as C, and supplying a spawn() that evaluated in-process returned implementation_provenance 'observed' for impl-c-derive with no C anywhere. The same shape held in the film plane against the real C binary's genuine digest. What actually held was 'authority read bytes X, then invoked callback Y'. Frozen as P-3 and P-3F in probe_execlaunch_v09_repro.mjs.
attrs.statement: EXECUTOR EXISTENCE IS NOT EXECUTION PROVENANCE. Proving that an executor exists — even proving which bytes it is made of — says nothing about which bytes came back from which request. An observation must bind the EXECUTOR, the REQUEST and the RETURNED BYTES as one execution event, and acceptance must take no part of that proof from its caller. This is round 17's issuance lesson one level higher: there, don't authenticate the grant, authenticate the WHOLE REQUEST; here, don't authenticate the executor handle, authenticate the WHOLE EXECUTION EVENT. So: manual registration is DELETED; the authority is the thing that runs an executor (execute(req, launcher)); a launcher supplies MECHANISM AND NO IDENTITY — where the artifact's files are and how to start them — and the authority reads and hashes those files itself, resolves the family name from its own digest→name POLICY, spawns, sends that request, takes those bytes, and only then records an observation keyed by H(request_sem_id | canonical(the whole result)); and accept(registry, req, res) consults that privately held table, so a relabelled result MISSES the observation rather than being compared against it. THREE IDENTITIES, because one string was answering three questions: implementation_family_id (what implementation this is), executable_artifact_id (H of the bytes the authority read), and executor_session_id (this particular authority-driven launch). The naming policy is not an observation — it says what bytes are CALLED, never that anything ran — and it is injective in both directions so a caller cannot rewrite it mid-run. DECLARED OPEN, stated conservatively on purpose: hashing a path and then spawning that path supports 'the host observed artifact X immediately before requesting execution of path P'. It is NOT a proof that the OS executed those exact bytes under every filesystem race, and it is not hardware-attested executable identity. Also uncovered: the node binary and standard library for a JS executor, and every shared object the loader binds for a native one.

attrs.evidence: probe_execlaunch_v09_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against verbatim frozen v0.8.0 copies — P-3, where a genuine JS artifact declaration plus an unrelated spawn() yields implementation_provenance 'observed' for impl-c-derive-v0.8.0 against the real JS closure digest; and P-3F, which RUNS the film-plane version against the real ic32_film binary's genuine digest and a run() that returns a film produced earlier, so no C process executes during the observation and film_provenance is still 'observed'. P-3F is the cleanest statement of the separation this project has been building: the film IS semantically valid, replaySemFilm proves it, and the claimed execution provenance is false. 5/5 confined live: no launcher parameter on either path, a catalog entry that carries no action and whose entrypoint must lie inside its own hashed closure, an invocation refused as non-canonical when it carries a function, a catalog that cannot be edited after construction, and sessions reported as a list. derive_realm_battery.mjs 20/20, derive_battery.mjs 45/45, bridge/film_check.mjs 14/14.
attrs.statement: ARTIFACT OBSERVATION DOES NOT ESTABLISH EXECUTION PROVENANCE UNLESS THE MECHANISM INVOKED IS MECHANICALLY DERIVED FROM THE ARTIFACT OBSERVED. Equivalently, and this is the operative form: a launch descriptor may not carry both the evidence and an independent executable action. @1 let the caller pick the label, @2 let it pick the name a registration would report, @3 made the authority hash real bytes and then call a function the caller had supplied beside them. Each revision closed one supplier and left the next; the pattern is that any field a caller controls on the launch path becomes the provenance. So the caller supplies NOTHING on that path. ObservedExecutionHost is constructed with an IMMUTABLE EXECUTOR CATALOG — family name to {kind, entrypoint, artifact_closure}, deep-frozen, injective, refusing an entrypoint outside its own hashed closure and refusing any entry field beyond those three. The transport for each kind is written in the host. execute(registry, req) names a family and nothing else; the invocation is DATA and is canonicalised, which refuses a function outright. Both authorities — derivation and film — share this host and share no semantics with it: it cannot re-derive a result, replay a film, or say what either means. Duplicating the semantic boundary is the fence; duplicating the mechanism reproduced the defect in both planes, which is how it was found twice. Acceptance reports executor_sessionS, plural. The key is over BYTES, so two launches producing byte-identical output share it; reporting a single session id claims a uniqueness the key cannot support, and @3's implementation overwrote the earlier record besides. DECLARED OPEN, unchanged: hash-then-launch supports 'the host observed artifact X immediately before requesting execution of path P'. It is NOT a proof that the OS executed those exact bytes under every filesystem race, and it is not hardware-attested executable identity. The node binary, its flags and the standard library are uncovered for a JS entry; every shared object the loader binds is uncovered for a native one.

attrs.evidence: lowering.mjs 0.2.0 freezes INPUT_PORT_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, inputsSemId, portSemId and INSTANTIATION_RECEIPT_FIELDS, with instantiate() throwing instantiate-not-implemented. LOWERING_SEM_ID MOVED as a consequence and that is the point: LOWERING_SPEC carries inputs_model, so deciding the model changes the lowering relation, and an id that survived the ruling unchanged would be claiming the decision was not part of the relation. lowering_check.mjs case 'out-of-fragment-refused' asserts decided true, implemented false, three DECLARED falsifiers, and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID distinct from LOWERING_SEM_ID; 9/9 with the refinement witness unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED. THE THREE FALSIFIERS ARE DECLARED AND NONE IS WRITTEN -- I-4a allocation-invariance, I-4b source-name-sensitivity, I-4c binding-has-force -- so this law is PROPERTY-TESTED for the DECISION and its refusal surface, and carries NO claim about instantiation behaviour, which does not exist yet. B2 writes the three.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B1.1 and kept as history. Revision 1 shipped an OVERBOUND identity projection -- LOWERING_SEM_ID and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID hashed lifecycle fields, so implementing a frozen relation would have re-identified it -- and an EXTRA-INPUT REFUSAL that contradicted the source evaluator, justified by a claim about functions that is false. Both were correct-looking and wrong; the architecture they sat on was right and is unchanged in @2.
attrs.statement: INSTANTIATION IS A SEPARATE RELATION FROM LOWERING AND CARRIES ITS OWN IDENTITY. A target template can be perfectly lowered while instantiation binds "x" to the port for "y". Merge the two relations and a target failure becomes ambiguous between A MISTRANSLATED PROGRAM and CORRECTLY TRANSLATED CODE WITH MISWIRED INPUTS, which is the class of ambiguity this record has spent twenty-seven rounds removing. So: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id, reusable and independent of invocation data; then target_template_sem_id + inputs_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, the closed executable term. The earlier framing, PARAMETERIZED versus INSTANTIATED, was a FALSE CHOICE: the template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed. instantiation_sem_id IDENTIFIES THE RELATION AND NOT THE INVOCATION -- it commits to the input-port namespace and version, the source-name-to-port rule, missing- and extra-input semantics, the canonical embedding of an input value, template substitution semantics, the refusal vocabulary and the conformance vectors, and it does NOT contain x=5, which is inputs_sem_id. THE PORT IS BOUND TO THE SOURCE NAME: port identity is H(namespace | canonicalBytes(source_input_name)), taken at the canonical target-AST layer as {op:"input-port", source_name:N} BEFORE any textual or ic32 variable allocation, so two implementations that internally allocate _impl17 and q93 reach the SAME target_template_sem_id. The quotient is exact and it is the INVERSE OF ROUND 16: internal target variable names are non-semantic and alpha-equivalent, source input keys are semantic. Round 16's bug was identity depending on a spelling that should not matter; the danger here is identity depending on an ALLOCATION that should not matter while losing the SOURCE NAME that must. SOURCE INPUT NAMES ARE NOT UNICODE-NORMALIZED: if the frozen core distinguishes two code-point sequences as different names, port identity preserves that exact distinction, because normalizing at the encoding layer is a language-semantic change made where the source cannot see it. INSTANTIATION GETS NO FILM -- it is a deterministic relation, not a transition system, so its instrument is independent RE-INSTANTIATION against an InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the same argument that gives lowering re-lowering. DECIDED, NOT BUILT, and the two states are distinguishable by name: `input` refuses as lower-input-not-implemented rather than lower-inputs-undecided, because a refusal that conflates 'we have not ruled' with 'we have ruled and not written it' is a stale instrument with a delay fuse.

CORRECTED AT B1.1, TWICE, AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE PART OF THE LAW. (1) A SEMANTIC IDENTITY MAY NOT HASH LIFECYCLE. B1's first cut hashed the whole spec, so flipping `implemented` from false to true moved LOWERING_SEM_ID from lsem-5673108765b4 to lsem-63f98923ed13 without one rule changing, and rewording the conformance-test STATUS sentence moved INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID. B2 becoming BUILT would therefore have re-identified a relation B1 froze -- round 16's defect arriving inside the compiler specification. The split is SEMANTICS (what the relation does; changing it changes emitted terms or accepted inputs) versus STATUS (rounds, evidence grades, whether code exists), and only the first is hashed, under new TRVM-*-SEM-v2 domain tags. The overbound B1 ids are KEPT as OVERBOUND_TRANSITIONAL_SEM_IDS rather than erased. DECLARED OPEN and not solved: the semantic records are still English, and rewording normative prose such as dup_label_policy or substitution still moves an id; a formal target-AST grammar would close that and is not written. (2) EXTRA CANONICAL INPUTS ARE IGNORED, NOT REFUSED, AND THE ORIGINAL ARGUMENT WAS FALSE. B1 froze extra inputs as instantiate-extra-input on the reasoning that accepting them would let inputs_sem_id vary while target_term_sem_id did not, 'so the receipt would stop being a function'. A function may be many-to-one; (template, {x:2}) and (template, {x:2, unused:999}) mapping to one term IS a function. Worse, the rule contradicted the source: evaluate({op:'input',name:'x'}, {}, {x:2, y:999}) returns 2, so refusing extras at the target would have broken refinement BY CONSTRUCTION on the first program carrying a spare input. Different inputs_sem_id mapping to the same target_term_sem_id is the correct statement that executable semantics do not depend on unused data. Narrowing the source's input discipline is a SOURCE-LANGUAGE change requiring a new CORE_SEM_ID, and the instantiator may not impose it unilaterally. THE REFINEMENT CLAIM IS SCOPED BEFORE IT IS MADE: it holds over canonical, fully bound input environments in which instantiation succeeds. Missing inputs are refused on BOTH sides but at different layers under different codes -- program-input-missing during source evaluation, instantiate-missing-input before any target term exists -- so SOURCE-REFUSAL to INSTANTIATION-REFUSAL preservation is a separate theorem and is DECLARED OPEN. AND I-4c MANDATES AN ASYMMETRIC FIXTURE: add(input(x), input(y)) with x=2,y=3 gives 5 under the correct binding and 5 under the swap, so the obvious witness is green whether or not the binding was honoured. The mandated fixture is add(input(x), add(input(x), input(y))) with x=2,y=3, which gives 7 correctly and 8 swapped. COMPLETED AT B1.2, because @2 froze an architecture the compiler could not express. lower() emitted an ic32 STRING, so there was no canonical target-AST layer for {op:'input-port'} to live at and a port could only have become a placeholder like $input_x -- spelling as semantics, the very defect this law forbids, reintroduced by the absence of the representation it presumes. THE CODOMAIN OF LOWERING IS A TEMPLATE: TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1, grammar church(n) | add(Template, Template) | port(source_name), with its own content-bound encoding identity. A TEMPLATE CONTAINS NO BINDER NAMES AND NO DUP LABELS -- emit() invents both from the template's shape by the declared depth-first policy -- so I-4a is a property of the DATA STRUCTURE and not a convention an emitter is asked to respect: there is no field an allocation could occupy. emit() REFUSES a template still holding a port (emit-unbound-port), because a template with a free port is not an executable term. The LoweringReceipt therefore ends at target_template_sem_id, not target_term_sem_id; a receipt ending at the term keeps asserting that lowering produced the executable term, which this law denies. AND THE HASHED SEMANTICS NOW CARRY THE WHOLE SOURCE FRAGMENT INCLUDING `input`: @2 left it out of lowered_ops, so B2 adding it would have moved LOWERING_SEM_ID -- implementing a frozen rule re-identifying the relation, which is exactly what the B1.1 correction set out to prevent. The rule is frozen ({op:'input',name:N} lowers to {t:'port',source_name:N}, N carried through unchanged) and the implementation is absent, and lower-input-not-implemented is a STATUS refusal that is deliberately NOT in refusal_semantics. Measured: implementing the input rule AND flipping both lifecycle flags moves neither semantic id.

INSTANTIATION GETS NO FILM -- it is a deterministic relation, not a transition system, so its instrument is independent RE-INSTANTIATION against an InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the same argument that gives lowering re-lowering. DECIDED, NOT BUILT, and the two states are distinguishable by name: `input` refuses as lower-input-not-implemented rather than lower-inputs-undecided, because a refusal that conflates 'we have not ruled' with 'we have ruled and not written it' is a stale instrument with a delay fuse. DECLARED OPEN and not solved: the semantic records are still English, and rewording normative prose such as dup_label_policy or substitution still moves an id; a formal target-AST grammar would close that and is not written. Each list now belongs to the record that owns it, and every name lowering claims is driven to a refusal by the witness. BUILT AT B2, AND BUILDING IT MOVED NEITHER SEMANTIC ID -- the property B1.1 split the records to make possible and the first round able to exercise it. `input` lowers to a structural port, instantiate() closes a template against canonical inputs, both lifecycle flags are true and all three port falsifiers are WITNESSED; none of that moved lsem or isem, and the measurement is an EQUATION rather than a simulation: put back only op_lowering_rules and only emission and the B1.2.1 identities return EXACTLY, so those two fields are the only hashed bytes the round touched. Merge the two relations and a target failure becomes ambiguous between A MISTRANSLATED PROGRAM and CORRECTLY TRANSLATED CODE WITH MISWIRED INPUTS, which is the class of ambiguity this record has spent twenty-seven rounds removing. So: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id, reusable and independent of invocation data; then target_template_sem_id + inputs_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, the closed executable term. The earlier framing, PARAMETERIZED versus INSTANTIATED, was a FALSE CHOICE: the template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed. instantiation_sem_id IDENTIFIES THE RELATION AND NOT THE INVOCATION -- it commits to the input-port namespace and version, the source-name-to-port rule, missing- and extra-input semantics, the canonical embedding of an input value, template substitution semantics, the refusal vocabulary and the conformance vectors, and it does NOT contain x=5, which is inputs_sem_id. THE PORT IS BOUND TO THE SOURCE NAME: port identity is H(namespace | canonicalBytes(source_input_name)), taken at the canonical target-AST layer as {op:"input-port", source_name:N} BEFORE any textual or ic32 variable allocation, so two implementations that internally allocate _impl17 and q93 reach the SAME target_template_sem_id. The quotient is exact and it is the INVERSE OF ROUND 16: internal target variable names are non-semantic and alpha-equivalent, source input keys are semantic. Round 16's bug was identity depending on a spelling that should not matter; the danger here is identity depending on an ALLOCATION that should not matter while losing the SOURCE NAME that must. SOURCE INPUT NAMES ARE NOT UNICODE-NORMALIZED: if the frozen core distinguishes two code-point sequences as different names, port identity preserves that exact distinction, because normalizing at the encoding layer is a language-semantic change made where the source cannot see it. INSTANTIATION GETS NO FILM -- it is a deterministic relation, not a transition system, so its instrument is independent RE-INSTANTIATION against an InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the same argument that gives lowering re-lowering. DECIDED, NOT BUILT, and the two states are distinguishable by name: `input` refuses as lower-input-not-implemented rather than lower-inputs-undecided, because a refusal that conflates 'we have not ruled' with 'we have ruled and not written it' is a stale instrument with a delay fuse. B1's first cut hashed the whole spec, so flipping `implemented` from false to true moved LOWERING_SEM_ID from lsem-5673108765b4 to lsem-63f98923ed13 without one rule changing, and rewording the conformance-test STATUS sentence moved INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID. B2 becoming BUILT would therefore have re-identified a relation B1 froze -- round 16's defect arriving inside the compiler specification. The split is SEMANTICS (what the relation does; changing it changes emitted terms or accepted inputs) versus STATUS (rounds, evidence grades, whether code exists), and only the first is hashed, under new TRVM-*-SEM-v2 domain tags. The overbound B1 ids are KEPT as OVERBOUND_TRANSITIONAL_SEM_IDS rather than erased. DECLARED OPEN and not solved: the semantic records are still English, and rewording normative prose such as dup_label_policy or substitution still moves an id; a formal target-AST grammar would close that and is not written. (2) EXTRA CANONICAL INPUTS ARE IGNORED, NOT REFUSED, AND THE ORIGINAL ARGUMENT WAS FALSE. THIS SENTENCE SAID 'SIX' AND OMITTED target_template_sem_id for the whole of B1.2, the pass that introduced it as an independently identified semantic object -- so the law, and the anti-collapse witness reading it, made a six-way claim about a seven-node chain and were green throughout. The enumeration now lives in REFINEMENT_CHAIN with an exercised flag per node and the witness DERIVES its set from it, because a hand-typed count drifting from the thing it counts is a species this tree has now caught in a law count, a case count, a rung count and here. Collapsing any pair turns a refinement statement into a renaming, which is the failure mode this whole chain is built to avoid. BUILT AT B2, AND BUILDING IT MOVED NEITHER SEMANTIC ID -- the property B1.1 split the records to make possible and the first round able to exercise it. `input` lowers to a structural port, instantiate() closes a template against canonical inputs, both lifecycle flags are true and all three port falsifiers are WITNESSED; none of that moved lsem or isem, and the measurement is an EQUATION rather than a simulation: put back only op_lowering_rules and only emission and the B1.2.1 identities return EXACTLY, so those two fields are the only hashed bytes the round touched. THE SOURCE-TO-TEMPLATE MAP IS STRUCTURAL AND INTERPRETED: lower() reads op_lowering_rules rather than carrying a second hand-coded copy of it, so a rule cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving LOWERING_SEM_ID. English rules beside a hand-coded implementation are two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed -- the codomain-in-prose defect one layer in -- and `transform: identity` on the port's source name is the no-normalization ruling made structural rather than stated. LOWER() NO LONGER RETURNS AN EXECUTABLE TERM. The convenience field was a SECOND PATH: the official route through instantiate() beside a shortcut through lowering, with every future reader having to remember which carried the semantics, which is how a hidden second mechanism returns. It is removed and the equality survives as a REGRESSION THEOREM -- instantiate(template, {}) reproduces the exact 129 bytes, the same six-frame film, the same normal form and the same 5. AND instantiate() MAY NOT MINT THE IDENTITY OF ITS OWN OUTPUT: an instantiator that emitted bytes and certified their semantic id would produce the artifact and the certificate from one source, so a wrong emission would carry a matching id and verify against itself. The kernel canonicalises the bytes; the receipt is built around that id; verification RE-INSTANTIATES and RE-CANONICALISES independently rather than asking the instantiator to agree with itself. THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER MOVED TO STATUS and gained two conditions: split emission into its own relation when it becomes independently REUSED, independently THEOREM-BEARING, independently VERSIONED OR REPLACEABLE, or when the closed-template intermediate becomes an independently IDENTIFIED or EXTERNALLY OBSERVED artifact. The last two fire first -- the moment two emitters are compared over one closed template, an emitter upgrade re-cutting the semantic identity of PORT SUBSTITUTION is plainly wrong. Keeping that trigger inside the hashed semantics, as B1.2.1 did, re-committed B1.1's own finding: governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when it is reworded. STILL DECLARED OPEN: source-refusal to instantiation-refusal preservation, unchanged. CORRECTED AND SPLIT AT B2.1. THREE THINGS, AND THE FIRST IS A DEFECT. (1) THE INSTANTIATOR MAY NOT READ ITS ARGUMENTS TWICE. B2's instantiate() read the caller's inputs once to BIND values into the term and again to compute inputs_sem_id, so a getter answering 2 and then 999 produced a term meaning x=2 beside an identity committing to {x:999} -- an application record asserting 'these inputs were {x:999}' above 'this term represents x=2'. Nothing about the runtime was wrong: the RELATION misbound its own input identity. That is derivation.entry-snapshot@1 arriving in the compiler layer, and the repair is the same mechanism: ONE canonical snapshot of BOTH arguments at entry, everything downstream reading the snapshot. THE INVARIANT: the bytes inputs_sem_id identifies are exactly the bytes from which every substituted value was derived. (2) A CLOSED VOCABULARY OF BARE NAMES STILL HIDES SEMANTICS. B2's rule table named predicates and transforms and bound each name to a JavaScript function, so redefining `integer` from Number.isInteger to always-true made const(1.5) lower successfully instead of refusing WITH LOWERING_SEM_ID UNCHANGED, and `identity` could have been made to normalize a source input name, silently undoing the port ruling. The vocabulary stays CLOSED and its DEFINITIONS are now data hashed into the relation; a rule may not name a predicate by JavaScript reference or by a bare string resolved elsewhere, and when the core exports reusable semantic predicates a rule references one by its predicate_sem_id. The kind interpreter is trusted code like canonicalBytes: what has been removed is the rule LANGUAGE's ability to hide meaning. (3) THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER FIRED, AND B2 TRIPPED ALL FOUR CONDITIONS AT ONCE. emit() is exported and independently reused; I-4a is a theorem about EMISSION ALONE, comparing two emitters over one template; the executable encoding carries its own content identity and an alternate emitter was deliberately run against it; and instantiate() RETURNED the closed template to its caller. The condition that settles it is the second: once two emitters are compared over one closed template, an emitter upgrade re-cutting the semantic identity of PORT SUBSTITUTION is plainly wrong, which is exactly what a merged relation does. So INSTANTIATION ENDS AT A CLOSED TEMPLATE and EMISSION is a third relation with EMISSION_SEM_ID: program -(lowering)-> template -(instantiation + inputs)-> CLOSED TEMPLATE -(emission)-> target term -(native film)-> normal form -(decode)-> outcome. The closed template carries its OWN IDENTITY DOMAIN, ctmpl- against tmpl-, EVEN WHERE ITS BYTES EQUAL AN OPEN TEMPLATE'S: for a program with no inputs the two structures are byte-identical and they are not the same thing -- one is what the COMPILER produced and the other is what an INVOCATION closed, and sharing an id would make 'this was instantiated' and 'this needed no instantiation' indistinguishable. Two receipts, each verified by recomputation of its OWN relation and neither filmed: InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, closed_template_sem_id} and EmissionReceipt {closed_template_sem_id, emission_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}. THE SPLIT MADE THE VERIFIERS CLEANER, which is an argument for it rather than a consequence: verifying instantiation needs NO runtime canonicaliser at all, because the relation now ends at a structure the module owns, and only emission needs one -- which it TAKES AS A PARAMETER, because the module that defines a relation must not also choose the oracle that judges it. Both verifiers are production functions; at B2 the only implementation of 'does this receipt hold?' lived in the test suite, and a relation whose verification procedure exists only in its own tests is a relation nobody else can check. B7 CARRIES `sub` THROUGH THE WHOLE CHAIN AND ADDS A SECOND DIRECTION TO THE CLAIM. The emitting side is the same eleven-node chain at the same grade -- sub(const 5, const 2) lowers, instantiates, emits 165 bytes of real predecessor structure, is filmed natively over 96 frames spanning APP-LAM, APP-SUP, DUP-LAM and DUP-SUP= with 66 dup-plane loci, replayed by the kernel on two runtime classes, normalised, decoded to 3, and agreed with by the source evaluator. THIS IS THE FIRST REFINEMENT WITNESS THAT IS ALSO A DUP-PLANE TERM: add(const 2, const 3) films six APP-LAM frames at tree loci and fires no dup rule at all, so until B7 the refinement chain and the runtime frontier were exercised by different fixtures. THE ASSOCIATION PAIR SHOWS THE TEMPLATE SHAPE IS SEMANTIC: (7-2)-1 and 7-(2-1) share three literals and one operator, lower to different templates, emit different terms and decode to 4 and 6 -- so nothing between source and target flattens, reassociates, or pre-inverts an operand pair. The ONE inversion the target needs (the subtrahend is the numeral applied) lives inside emit() and nowhere else. AND THE OTHER DIRECTION IS NOW PART OF THE CLAIM RATHER THAN AN OMISSION: three unrepresentable programs LOWER and INSTANTIATE and are refused only at EMISSION as emit-sub-underflow, while the source evaluator returns -1, 1 and -3. That is a CODOMAIN refusal -- source language properly contains the representable target fragment -- and NOT refusal preservation, which remains DECLARED OPEN and untouched. REFINEMENT_SCOPE.representable_only records the distinction so the two cannot be confused later. AND B7 TRIPPED A RATCHET IN THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN IN THE RECORD: two cases drove lower-unsupported-op with a hard-typed {op:"sub"} and both FAILED the moment sub lowered. The driver is now DERIVED from CORE_SPEC.ops minus IMPLEMENTED_LOWERED_OPS minus the read family, with a null driver counted as a FAILURE rather than a skip -- repointing it at the next unlowered op would have rebuilt the identical trap for whichever round widens next.

attrs.statement: MULTIPLICITY MUST PRESERVE CORRELATION. EVIDENCE FIELDS THAT VARY TOGETHER MAY NOT BE INDEPENDENTLY COLLAPSED INTO SINGULAR SUMMARIES. Round 24 established that the observation key is over BYTES, so two launches producing byte-identical output share it, and made executor_sessions plural so that one id would stop being reported as though it named the launch in hand. It is the database error of selecting one column from the first row and another column from all rows and presenting the pair as a record. THE TUPLE IS THE UNIT: observations are grouped by the (implementation_family_id, executable_artifact_id) that actually co-occurred, carrying the sessions that ran it, and every singular field is DERIVED -- emitted only when genuinely unique and null otherwise, which is what the family id has done since round 24 and what the artifact id should have done alongside it. attrs.statement: UNTRUSTED DATA MUST BE SEVERED BEFORE IT IS VALIDATED, NOT VALIDATED BEFORE IT IS SEVERED. Every untrusted structure that becomes authority state is canonicalised into an OWNED SNAPSHOT exactly once; validation, identity computation and storage then operate only on that snapshot. NO UNOWNED MUTABLE OBJECT IS CONSULTED TWICE ACROSS A TRUST DECISION. A getter is read as many times as it is written, and the reads need not agree. v0.11.0's executor catalog read `entrypoint` four times — typeof, isAbsolute, the entrypoint-inside-closure check, and then the frozen internal entry — so a getter answering honestly for the three validating reads and maliciously for the fourth put an entrypoint OUTSIDE its own hashed closure into the immutable catalog, and the un-hashed executable really ran while acceptance reported the honest closure's digest. ProgramRegistry.bind had the same shape with a milder outcome: it hashed the caller's AST and then cloned it, so the registry could be keyed by const(5)'s identity while holding const(999). THE MILDER OUTCOME IS NOT A DEFENCE. bind fails closed only because verify() recomputes the id from what was stored — a SECOND mechanism catching the first is not the first working, and authorize() will issue a request against the broken id in the meantime. This is the sixth rung, and the first that is not an object: @1 the implementation LABEL, @2 the registration NAME, @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence, @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE, @5 the AUTHORITY-BEARING OBJECT, @6 MUTABLE DATA READ TWICE. canonicalBytes has refused a capability since v0.1.0; what was not said is that reading THROUGH it twice reintroduces one — the second read IS the capability. The executor catalog is canonical PLAIN DATA only, and a Map is refused: this is a trust boundary whose thesis is that capabilities are not data, and admitting richer JS object forms at it buys nothing.

attrs.evidence: negative_battery.sh: establish_baseline() runs grid_check on the unperturbed fixture and refuses the whole run if it does not exit 0, printing that no case below is isolated-cause evidence. The baseline is established once because every case builds its fixture by the same recipe from the same source — and that is VERIFIED rather than assumed: each case compares its own pre-perturbation digest against the baselined tree and fails FIXTURE DRIFT otherwise. harness_selftest.sh M-9 keeps the species in the bounded nine. Paired probes satisfy the convention by construction, since their live half IS the baseline and must be confined for the probe to pass. DECLARED OPEN: the one-directional 9D probes (maintainer, coordinator_alias, realm, ownfailopen, closureenv) assert a breach without first asserting that the honest fixture holds the invariants they attack; their baselines are not yet established in code. The runner half is EXECUTABLE as runner_contract.sh, 3/3: a throwaway make target built from the governance recipe form itself must succeed on a subject that exits 0, and fail on a subject that exits 1 and on a subject that crashes without printing. Deliberately NOT a tenth harness species — the nine are about falsifier non-vacuity, and process-status propagation is a different layer: whether the runner can hear the subject at all.
attrs.statement: A perturbation-based result is admissible only if the IDENTICAL verifier, fixture, environment and artifact set satisfy their DECLARED baseline before the perturbation is applied. The word is DECLARED, not silent: each falsifier family names what its own clean state looks like. The negative battery's baseline is grid_check exiting 0 on the unperturbed fixture; the C bridge's is 48/48 byte equality; the kernel's is the canonical certificate and gates matching; a World attack probe's is the honest fixture satisfying the World invariants it is about to attack. Every perturbation harness implements five phases in order: establish_baseline, perturb, assert_perturbation (non-vacuity and target-match), run_subject, assert_specific_diagnostic. POSITIVE gates — kernel, World, bridge — need no additional 'must report nothing' test, because they ARE baseline observations. What needs this invariant is any claim of the form 'I changed X and therefore X caused this failure', which is exactly what a negative case asserts. Between round 14 and round 17 the negative battery's baseline was red and no case was isolated-cause evidence; nothing was falsely green, and that is a different and weaker property than the one the roster was reporting. AND A GATE MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL. A runner that pipes its subject into another command takes the exit status of the PIPE, not of the subject, so a gate whose subject CRASHED prints a stack trace's last line and reports success. Every governance recipe therefore captures its subject's output and status before printing, and the failure is verified in both directions: an unresolvable import and a failing assertion must each fail the target.

attrs.evidence: harness_selftest.sh, 9/9. attrs.statement: The apparatus is measured by a gate, not by attention. law:evidence.instrument-nonvacuity@1 requires each falsifier to be non-vacuous; this requires the HARNESS ITSELF to demonstrate that it detects the failure species that have actually occurred in this tree. Nine are enumerated and each has a meta-falsifier: working-directory dependence, an absent declared artifact, a present undeclared artifact, a perturbation that changes nothing, a case that DELETES rather than modifies, a case that moves an artifact it did not declare, a case whose expected diagnostic is not the one produced, a paired probe whose frozen side has been silently repaired, and — the one a battery of forgeries cannot see — an UNPERTURBED case tree that does not pass the checker. attrs.evidence: negative_battery.sh computes a pre- and post-perturbation digest of every scratch tree and refuses to credit a case whose forgery changed nothing (diagnostic: VACUOUS). This law is retrospective as much as prospective: it covers the unset $SCRATCH that meant a case could never execute, the hand-typed 44/44 that stopped counting the cases, the hard-coded "1.0.2" replacement that a version bump would have turned into a no-op, the prototype half of the authority graph that went untested, the false '9D-4 confined' produced by poisoning a node whose semantic path the pass overwrote, and a probe line that printed 'directly assignable' while testing typeof === 'function'. Six apparatus failures across four rounds, every one of which this rule would have caught mechanically. MECHANISED (both runners, v1.14.0): clause 1 — the intended target is DERIVED from the perturbation script (files opened for writing, files removed) and must EQUAL the set that actually changed, so a case editing the wrong artifact, or an extra one, fails as loudly as one editing nothing; clauses 2-3 — per-file digests before and after, refusing VACUOUS and naming the artifact perturbed; clause 5 — the specific diagnostic must match; clause 6 — CAUGHT increments only after all of the above. Both detectors were verified to FIRE by deliberately breaking a case (VACUOUS: 57/58; TARGET MISMATCH: 63/64) and restoring it. attrs.statement: An audit result is creditable only if the instrument independently proves that the intended perturbation occurred, the intended execution path was exercised, and the measured predicate is the one reported. A falsifier that forges nothing, runs nothing, or measures a different predicate than it names is VACUOUS, and a vacuous falsifier is worse than an absent one because the roster still counts it. Mutation cases must show before_hash != after_hash before the detector's verdict counts.

attrs.statement: HISTORY MAY BE PINNED. LIVE STATE MUST BE DERIVED. An instrument whose intended subject is the LIVE, CURRENT or CANONICAL state may not LOCATE or CHARACTERISE that subject with a literal belonging to one phase -- a revision number, a version string, a count, or a boolean polarity. An instrument whose subject genuinely IS history may and SHOULD pin it, because deriving a historical subject makes it stop testing history; that case declares itself with an explicit exemption carrying a reason. THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENCE, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDS A GUARD OF ITS OWN. A phase-pinned case is not VACUOUS -- a superseded revision still exists, so the mutation really changes a file -- and its declared TARGET still matches, and the clean baseline is still clean. Every other apparatus check passes. The case has simply stopped testing the thing it names, and the two available outcomes are a failure that reads like an engine defect, or nothing at all when a neighbouring assertion happens to catch the mutation anyway. FOUR INSTANCES IN TWO ROUNDS EARNED THIS LAW, and they are recorded rather than summarised because the shape is easier to recognise than to define: (1) grid_check required lowering_spike.inputs_model.implemented === false, correct while the port was open and, once B2 built it, the mechanism preventing the record from admitting the port had closed -- four passes stale; (2) the negative case guarding it forged implemented=True and expected 'must stay false', so the BATTERY enforced the stale value and 298/298 stayed green over a record contradicting the code; (3) grid_check selected the canonical film law by revision === 3, hand-edited on every supersession; (4) three battery cases selected revision == 3, and when @4 became canonical they went on mutating a superseded revision nothing asserts over and reported their own forgeries as UNCAUGHT. THE RULE IS NOT 'NO LITERALS IN EXPECTATIONS', which would be too blunt: implementation-provenance@1 must stay on the record AS a false claim, and film.native-emission@1 carries a readback record no later revision repeats. Those are correct BECAUSE they are pinned. The distinguishing question is what the instrument's SUBJECT is, not whether a number appears in it. AND THE CATALOGUE STAYS BOUNDED. This is the TENTH species in harness_selftest, added because the class repeated and not because it might; the guard is a narrow lint over the two negative runners, not a general analyzer for every way a test can be written badly. Ten, and then stop until an eleventh actually appears.

attrs.statement: THE EXECUTION PLANE ORIGINATES EVIDENCE, RATHER THAN THE GOVERNANCE PLANE RECONSTRUCTING IT AROUND THE EXECUTION PLANE AFTERWARDS. For a frozen one-step fixture, the native C runtime independently emits a semantic-film frame whose pre-state, enabled rule, canonical locus, post-state and terminal status are accepted by the existing TRVM-SEMFILM-v1.1 contract WITHOUT normalization or translation of meaning — the law kernel's own replaySemFilm, imported unmodified, replaying on a fresh runtime. Every field is derived by the emitter from its own execution: the redex is found by an enumeration that mirrors findAppRedexes over ic32's packed-word heap, the rule is the rule that fired, quiescence is the same enumeration run again and required to be empty, and the readback is required to be PURE (resolving the state must cost no interaction). SCOPE, checked rather than assumed: MULTI-FRAME films over APP-plane rules, on terms that may CARRY dup cells, C→JS only. v0.1.0 scoped itself by dup PRESENCE and that was the right refusal for the wrong reason — the lowered add(const 2, const 3) carries dup cells and, under the leftmost-tree-app strategy, fires none, so the blocker was ENABLEDNESS all along. A term where a DUP-* rule becomes enabled is REFUSED BY NAME (film-dup-rule-enabled); so is a term already in normal form; and the terminal re-checks pool-quiescence rather than inheriting it from the loop. STILL UNBUILT and named: the six DUP-* rules, the d: and v: loci, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED terminals. AND ONE CHECK WAS REMOVED BECAUSE IT WAS ACCIDENTALLY TRUE. v0.1.0 asserted the readback fired ZERO interactions; on a one-step dup-free fixture resolving the state costs nothing, so a machine counter that never moved looked like a verified property. ic32's `interactions` is not plane-classified, so comparing it against zero measures a different quantity from the kernel's INTERACT-plane claim — it fires four on the lowered term whose state is nonetheless correct. The count is now REPORTED and pool-quiescence is what is ASSERTED. The C-side checker — films flowing the other direction — is not claimed. A film arriving from outside is an execution CLAIM exactly as a DeriveResult is, so film provenance uses the same discipline as derivation.implementation-provenance@4: the shared ObservedExecutionHost, an immutable catalog entry naming the binary, hash-then-launch, and an observation keyed over the whole emission rather than over the film alone — provenance is over everything the executor emitted, not over a subset a caller chose to present. REPLAY AND PROVENANCE ARE REPORTED SEPARATELY, because a film can be semantically perfect and its claimed provenance false; P-3F is exactly that case. THE TWO TRANSITION SYSTEMS STAY SEPARATE (film_planes): the TRVM calculus film is pre-state → (rule + locus) → post-state over the ic32 interaction-net relation, and the derivation evidence relation is DeriveRequest → evaluate → DeriveResult. What is shared is HOST INFRASTRUCTURE, not semantics.

Enumeration covers the root tree AND EVERY LIVE DUP CELL; loci are canonical in three families -- t: a structural path, d: a DISCOVERY INDEX over live cells, v: a discovery index AND a path into a cell's value -- and the rules with a native handler are APP-LAM, APP-SUP, DUP-LAM, DUP-SUP=, DUP-SUP!, DUP-VAR and DUP-APP. THE TWO ORDERS ARE DIFFERENT ORDERS AND BOTH ARE LOAD-BEARING: the kernel enumerates live cells right-to-left (liveHeap pushes children forward) and INDEXES loci left-to-right (liveDiscoveryOrder pushes them reversed), so one order decides which redex is leftmost and the other decides what number its locus carries; collapsing either onto the other produces a locus that names a real redex which is not the redex that fired. SCOPE, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AND STATED AS REFUSALS: APP-ERA and DUP-ERA are ENUMERATED -- so that 'no enabled work' cannot silently mean 'no work of the kinds I implement', which is how a false normal form is written down -- and REFUSED BY NAME (film-era-rule-not-implemented) rather than fired, because neither has a witness; the church_exp_2_2 measurement is what established that this corpus fires NEITHER, correcting a plan that had expected only DUP-ERA to be missing.
